To begin with, in order to pre-evaluate the practicability of ether and carbonate ester as the electrolyte in pouch cells, comparative tests were first carried out, as shown in Fig. S1. Although the ether electrolytes have a high initial capacity, their cycling stability is poor, with a capacity retention rate of only 77.38 after 105 cycles, while the carbonate electrolytes have a capacity retention rate of 87.49 %. The gas production behaviour of ether and carbonate ester during long-term cycling at a cut-off voltage of 4.0 V at 45°C was monitored using differential electrochemical mass spectrometry (Fig. S2). It was observed that ether produced a greater quantity of gases, including methane and carbon monoxide, in comparison to carbonate ester. This may be a contributing factor to the unsuitability of ether for use in pouch cells, due to the rapid consumption of electrolyte, which results in a rapid decline in battery capacity. The electrolyte formula employs a combination of 1 mol/L NaPF $_{6}$ , cyclic ester EC and linear ester EMC in a mass ratio of 3:7 (called Baseline electrolyte), augmented by the incorporation of 3 wt% TMSS as a functional additive. The introduction of linear esters engenders a reduction in viscosity and an enhanced capacity to dissolve sodium salts in the electrolyte as a whole, thereby facilitating an improvement in the fluidity and ion conductivity of the electrolyte. Compounds containing sulfone groups, such as 1,3-propanesultone (PS), have been demonstrated to have excellent effects in inhibiting gas production and improving high-temperature performance (Fig. 1a). Consequently, they have been introduced into electrolytes and have become widely used. Compounds containing siloxane structures, such as trimethylsilyl isocyanate, exhibit high reactivity due to the facile rupture of their Si-O bonds. This enables effective removal of moisture and acid from the electrolyte and protection of the electrode electrolyte interface phase [25,26]. Therefore, the incorporation of TMSS is anticipated to combine the aforementioned effects with functional electrolytes, thereby achieving high-performance NFM/HC SIBs.

The potential function of TMSS in the electrolyte is also evaluated through DFT theoretical calculations. NaPF $_6$ was dissolved into a EC and EMC (EC: EMC = 3:7 in wt.%) mixture to prepare baseline electrolyte (1 mol/L). Trimethylsilyl methanesulfonate additive (97 %, Shanghai Macklin Biochemical Technology Co., Ltd.) was added into the baseline electrolyte to form functional electrolyte. The HC anode was contained 95 % HC, 1.5 % carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), 2.0 % styrene butadiene rubber (SBR), and 1.5 % super P. It is demonstrated that with the addition of TMSS in the electrolyte, three aspects can be effectively affected: i) Optimizing solvation structure to reduce desolvation energy, promote faster reaction kinetics and stabilize the electrolyte; ii) The formation of a high-quality S/Si-based CEI/SEI layer on the electrode surface has the effect of reducing both the sodium ion transport resistance and the deposition of dead sodium; iii) Capturing HF, removing trace amounts of water, reducing the volume expansion of material phase transitions, and ensuring the structural stability of the positive electrode material. The performance of the cells with TMSS was enhanced. This study offers novel insights into the design of functional electrolyte for commercial all-climate pouch SIBs with high energy density.

In this work, TDFP is firstly developed to design functional electrolytes and successfully achieve enhanced temperature performance of pouch NFM/HC cells. Compared to the NaDFP-containing electrolyte, the TDFP-containing electrolyte owns superior physical properties, and also can form much tougher SEI/CEI than that of TMSP. What's more, TDFP own a unique “formation-repair” film-formation behavior which induced rich-NaF SEI/CEI before/during charging. Benefit to these, the cycling stability of the cells with TDFP-containing electrolyte is considerably improved under the room and cold conditions, the capacity retention after 400 cycles at 25 °C increases from 0% to 90% and even stable cycling performance after 150 cycles can be obtained at 45 °C. In addition to the obtained functional electrolytes, this work also provides new insight for designing functional electrolytes of SIBs.

The effect of NaFSI on the redox properties of the electrolyte was first analyzed by electrochemical methods. Figure 1a shows the LSV curves of Na/Pt half cell, the addition of NaFSI resulted in a slight decrease in the oxidative resistance of the electrolyte, but much higher than the working voltage of the electrolyte, so NaFSI has no obvious negative impact on the actual working state of the electrolyte. Secondly, the influence of NaFSI on the reduction performance of the electrolyte was explored through the CV test of Na/HC half cell (Figure 1b, c). The oxidation/reduction peaks below 0.3 V correspond to the insertion/extraction of Li $^{+}$ . Because of the formation of SEI film on hard carbon in the battery with NaFSI, the rate of insertion/extraction of Li $^{+}$ slows down, as well as the current in the CV peaks at around 0.01 V decreases. It proves that NaFSI helps to form a protective film on the surface of HC in the initial cycles of the battery. Compared with the single salt system, after the addition of NaFSI, a huge reduction peak appeared from 1.0 V, and the peak current of the cell was significantly weakened, indicating that a passivation film was generated on the electrode surface. At the same time, with NaFSI, the coincidence between the second and third cycle of the CV curves are better than the blank one, indicating that the passivation film generated by NaFSI is stable and can maintain the stable cycling performance of SIBs.

The effect of sodium salts on the safety is also an important factor for commercial SIBs, and the corrosion of battery devices is one of the reference bases for sodium salt selection. Fig. 3e and f shows the corrosion results of Al foil in different electrolytes. As is reported at previous research, NaFSI-E would corrode Al foil during cycling so that may cause safety issues where NaDFOB-E and $\mathrm{NaPF_6 - E}$ hardly react. The coin cell was used to evaluate the corrosion of Al foil in different electrolytes. Surprisingly, although it can still observe obvious corrosion products on the glass fiber after cycling with NaFSI-E when measured with the coin cell, the Al foil inside the SIBs remains integrity, but the battery shell has obvious corrosion traces, as shown in Fig. 3g, which is quite different from the result measured by the electrolytic tank as shown in Fig. 3h. From this phenomenon, it can be inferred that NaFSI-E would corrode Al foil as well as stainless steel but corrode stainless steel first.

Battery performance is the most straightly and convincing evidence to evaluate the electrolytes with different sodium salts. At present stage, NFM and HC are widely considered as ideal cathode and anode materials for commercial pouch SIBs due to their duration to water and air $[23–26]$ . The electrochemical performance of NFM||HC pouch SIBs with various electrolytes including $NaPF_{6}$ , NaFSI and NaDFOB from $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ to $70\ ^{\circ}C$ , have been thoroughly investigated. The rate capability of the cells with different electrolytes at various current densities under $45\ ^{\circ}C$ was firstly studied, as illustrated in Fig. 4a. The $NaPF_{6}-E$ and NaFSI-E cells showed similar rate capabilities, while the NaDFOB-E cell exhibited inferior performance. Conversely, the cycling performance as shown in Fig. 4b indicated that the NaDFOB-E and NaFSI-E cells were more stable than the $NaPF_{6}-E$ cell, and following $70\ ^{\circ}C$ storage experiment results also confirmed that NaDFOB-E and NaFSI-E cells had better performance than $NaPF_{6}-E$ cell, as shown in Fig. 4c.

source_refs.raw_quote: The main raw materials used for preparing functional electrolytes, including ethylene carbonate (EC), ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC), sodium hexafluorophosphate $\left(\mathrm{NaPF}_{6}\right)$ , NaDFP, TMSP and TDFP were provided by the Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. The baseline electrolyte was prepared by dissolving $NaPF_{6}$ in a mixture of EC: EMC = 3:7 to form a concentration of 0.8 mol $L^{-1}$ . Then, 1% (Mass ratio) NaDFP, TDFP, TMSP was added into the baseline electrolyte to prepare corresponding electrolyte. All electrolytes were prepared in a dry argon filled glove box with both moisture and oxygen concentrations below 0.1 ppm. NFM was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co, Ltd., HC was purchased from Kuraray Co Ltd. The pouch test cells with NFM cathode (120 mAh $g^{-1}$ at 0.1C), HC anode (290 mAh $g^{-1}$ at 0.05C), and Celgard 2700 separator were assembled using the conventional assembly method. Thereinto, NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotube (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and Maleic acid were dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) with a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate to prepare the NFM cathode.

source_refs.raw_quote: This is likely attributable to the sharp decline in conductivity and the surge in viscosity caused by NaDFP at low temperatures, which weakened the electrolyte's kinetic performance and resulted in inferior rate performance compared to cells with TMSP and TDFP. Furthermore, performance tests were conducted at even lower temperatures, and it was found that the cells with TDFP still maintained an 86% discharge capacity retention rate at -30 °C. Low temperature cycling test is followed to further validate the superior performance of TDFP. As illustrated in Fig. 4d, the cell with TDFP exhibited the best cycling stability, followed by TMSP, then NaDFP, and finally the Baseline. It is worth noting that the performance of TMSP and NaDFP batteries under low-temperature cycling was the reverse of that under room-temperature cycling. This suggests that the failure mechanisms of the batteries and the reasons for performance enhancement by additives also differ. The thicknesses of cells haven't visible change before and after cycling, meaning no significant gas generation could be observed under low-temperature conditions (Fig. 4e). This contrasts with the results under room-temperature cycling, leading to the slightly better performance of TMSP-containing cells compared to NaDFP-containing cells under low-temperature conditions.

source_refs.raw_quote: Before the electrochemical tests, the pouch cells were subjected to an overnight aging and formation treatment. The formation step was an essential activation process for pouch SIBs, including the SIBs were first charged at room temperature to 2.0 V, and then charged at 45 °C (0.5 MPa) at a current of 90 mA to 3.8 V. The cycling tests were conducted on a battery test system (CT-4008-5V3A-FA model, Neware Technology Co., Ltd.) by charging at 0.9 A to 3.8 V and then holding at 3.8 V until the current drops to 30 mA, and then discharging at 0.9 A to 1.5 V. The charge and discharge rates of the low temperature cycle were 0.3C and 0.5C, respectively. CR2025 coin cells were assembled to assess the performance of Na/HC, HC/HC and NFM/NFM half-cells using the asprepared electrolytes and the glass fiber separator (Whatman GF/B). The electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) and cyclic voltammetry (CV) curves were performed by using solartron Analytical (CellTest1470, AMETEK Technology Co., Ltd.). In the galvanostatic intermittent titration technique (GITT) test, the charge and discharge current was 45 mA, the charging time was 30 min, and the shelving time was 5 h.

The HC anode was contained 95 % HC, 1.5 % carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), 2.0 % styrene butadiene rubber (SBR), and 1.5 % super P. A Celgard 2700 membrane (Xingyuan Materials Co., Ltd) was as the separator. The mass loading of cathode and anode was 33.0 mg cm $^{-2}$ and 20.1 mg cm $^{-2}$ , respectively. The negative-to-positive (N/P) capacity ratio was 1.1. The empty pouch cells were dried under vacuum at 80 °C for 72 h, then transferred to a glove box and injected 6.0 g electrolyte. Other operations not mentioned were all carried out using the general methods in the battery manufacture.

3.1. Design and performance of the functional electrolyte
To begin with, in order to pre-evaluate the practicability of ether and carbonate ester as the electrolyte in pouch cells, comparative tests were first carried out, as shown in Fig. S1. Although the ether electrolytes have a high initial capacity, their cycling stability is poor, with a capacity retention rate of only 77.38 after 105 cycles, while the carbonate electrolytes have a capacity retention rate of 87.49 %. The gas production behaviour of ether and carbonate ester during long-term cycling at a cut-off voltage of 4.0 V at 45°C was monitored using differential electrochemical mass spectrometry (Fig. S2). It was observed that ether produced a greater quantity of gases, including methane and carbon monoxide, in comparison to carbonate ester. This may be a contributing factor to the unsuitability of ether for use in pouch cells, due to the rapid consumption of electrolyte, which results in a rapid decline in battery capacity. The electrolyte formula employs a combination of 1 mol/L NaPF $_{6}$ , cyclic ester EC and linear ester EMC in a mass ratio of 3:7 (called Baseline electrolyte), augmented by the incorporation of 3 wt% TMSS as a functional additive. The introduction of linear esters engenders a reduction in viscosity and an enhanced capacity to dissolve sodium salts in the electrolyte as a whole, thereby facilitating an improvement in the fluidity and ion conductivity of the electrolyte. Compounds containing sulfone groups, such as 1,3-propanesultone (PS), have been demonstrated to have excellent effects in inhibiting gas production and improving high-temperature performance (Fig. 1a). Consequently, they have been introduced into electrolytes and have become widely used. Compounds containing siloxane structures, such as trimethylsilyl isocyanate, exhibit high reactivity due to the facile rupture of their Si-O bonds. This enables effective removal of moisture and acid from the electrolyte and protection of the electrode electrolyte interface phase [25,26]. Therefore, the incorporation of TMSS is anticipated to combine the aforementioned effects with functional electrolytes, thereby achieving high-performance NFM/HC SIBs.

The cycling performance of pouch NFM/HC cells with/without TMSS at 1C in the range of (e) 1.5–4.0 V at 25 °C and (f) 1.5–3.8 V at 45 °C. It is well established that sodium-ion batteries exhibit superior low-temperature performance compared to lithium-ion batteries. This attribute is of significant potential value for their future applications $[32]$ . Due to the sluggish interfacial kinetics, the energy density and cycle life of SIBs suffer severely at subzero temperatures $[33]$ . Consequently, the electrochemical performance of electrolytes with and without TMSS was evaluated at extreme temperatures. Fig. 3c illustrates that the electrolyte containing TMSS exhibited superior cycling stability and capacity retention compared to the baseline electrolyte at $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ with a 0.3C charge and 0.5C discharge. Batteries without TMSS exhibited a significant decline in capacity, retaining only 60% of their initial capacity after 40 cycles. This was attributed to their low coulombic efficiency and high polarization.

source_refs.raw_quote: A type of wide temperature range electrolyte design strategy incorporating trifunctional trimethylsilyl methanesulfonate (TMSS) additive in specific carbonate ester is developed to enhance the all-climate performance of commercial pouch $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). The incorporation of TMSS serves optimizing the solvation structure to accelerate the reaction kinetics, eliminating residual $H_{2}O/HF$ from the electrolyte, and promoting the formation of high-quality interface films. The capacity retention of the pouch NFM/HC cells with TMSS is effectively enhanced at high-voltage of 4.0 V and wide-temperature range from $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . The cell delivers a high capacity retention of 80 % after 700 cycles at $25\ ^{\circ}C$ , while the initial energy density is as high as 117 Wh kg $^{-1}$ and maintains 103 Wh kg $^{-1}$ after 300 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ and 1C (1C = 900 mA), achieving an 18.2 % increase in energy density. In addition, no obvious gas evolution can be observed when pouch cell is stored at $60\ ^{\circ}C$ and the low-temperature discharge at $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ achieves a 14.76 % increase in capacity at 0.5C. This work demonstrates the feasibility of TMSS in SIBs, and also put insight on the rational electrolyte design of SIBs.

source_refs.raw_quote: Based on the coupling of difluorophosphate-group with -tris(trimethylsilyl)-group of tris(trimethylsilyl)difluorophosphate (TDFP) additive and a “formation-repair” film-forming strategy, a difluorophosphate-based functional electrolyte is developed. This electrolyte facilitates the formation of tough and rich-NaF interfacial films on two electrodes and achieves an enhanced temperature performance of $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) over a wide range from $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . Compared to the cells without TDFP, the capacity retention of pouch NFM/HC cells with TDFP after 400 cycles at $25\ ^{\circ}C$ increases from 0% to 90%, stable cycling performance is obtained after 150 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ , and even the discharge capacity at $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ and the capacity retention after storage at $60\ ^{\circ}C$ are also greatly improved. In addition, the unique properties of TDFP differ from sodium difluorophosphate (NaDFP) and tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphate (TMSP) are analyzed to elucidate the functional mechanisms of TDFP. It is demonstrated that TDFP can not only catalyze the decomposition of $PF_{6}^{-}$ to form NaF-rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI)/cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI) films but also produce $PO_{2}F_{2}^{-}$ to optimize the film composition.

source_refs.raw_quote: This allows it to maintain good performance in low temperature conditions. During the charge and discharge process, TMSS is capable of capturing the HF generated by the hydrolysis of $PF_{6}^{-}$ in the solvent due to the presence of trace amounts of water. This protects the positive electrode material from corrosion and reduces the dissolution of transition metal ions. Additionally, the S = O group of the abundant charge carrier can stabilize $PF_{5}$ , reduce the opening of the solvent EC, and thus reduce the gas production of the pouch cells. This ensures that the battery will remain in good working order under conditions of high temperature. Moreover, TMSS exhibits a preferential oxidation and decomposition process, resulting in the formation of low impedance, high ion mobility CEI films and SEI films rich in S-based and Si-based compounds on the cathode and anode surfaces. These films have the capacity to inhibit the decomposition of $PF_{6}$ and improve the thermodynamic and kinetic stability of the electrolyte.

source_refs.raw_quote: Sodium salts in the electrolytes are key materials for developing high-performance sodium ion batteries (SIBs) due to their direct influences on the electrode reactions and electrolyte conductivity, and sodium fluorophosphate $(\mathrm{NaPF}_6)$ is known to be widely applied. Using $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ as a comparison, this work systematically evaluates the application potential of $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ , sodium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (NaFSI) and sodium difluoro(oxalato)borate (NaDFOB) from the sodium salt nature, electrolyte properties, and battery performance. It is demonstrated that NaFSI can exhibit excellent comprehensive performance and has the potential to substitute for $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ under certain conditions; NaDFOB is more suitable as an additive to improve the high-temperature performance of SIBs. In particular, $\mathrm{NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_2}$ /hard carbon (NFM/HC) SIBs with NaDFOB achieve enhanced performance than that with $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ at high temperature (from $88.2\%$ to $92.4\%$ ), while low temperature performance of NaFSI-containing cells is much better than others (from $0\%$ to $85.9\%$ ).

3.2. Performance of the batteries with different electrolytes
The effect of sodium salts on the safety is also an important factor for commercial SIBs, and the corrosion of battery devices is one of the reference bases for sodium salt selection. Fig. 3e and f shows the corrosion results of Al foil in different electrolytes. As is reported at previous research, NaFSI-E would corrode Al foil during cycling so that may cause safety issues where NaDFOB-E and $\mathrm{NaPF_6 - E}$ hardly react. The coin cell was used to evaluate the corrosion of Al foil in different electrolytes. Surprisingly, although it can still observe obvious corrosion products on the glass fiber after cycling with NaFSI-E when measured with the coin cell, the Al foil inside the SIBs remains integrity, but the battery shell has obvious corrosion traces, as shown in Fig. 3g, which is quite different from the result measured by the electrolytic tank as shown in Fig. 3h. From this phenomenon, it can be inferred that NaFSI-E would corrode Al foil as well as stainless steel but corrode stainless steel first.

Battery performance is the most straightly and convincing evidence to evaluate the electrolytes with different sodium salts. At present stage, NFM and HC are widely considered as ideal cathode and anode materials for commercial pouch SIBs due to their duration to water and air $[23–26]$ . The electrochemical performance of NFM||HC pouch SIBs with various electrolytes including $NaPF_{6}$ , NaFSI and NaDFOB from $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ to $70\ ^{\circ}C$ , have been thoroughly investigated. The rate capability of the cells with different electrolytes at various current densities under $45\ ^{\circ}C$ was firstly studied, as illustrated in Fig. 4a. The $NaPF_{6}-E$ and NaFSI-E cells showed similar rate capabilities, while the NaDFOB-E cell exhibited inferior performance. Conversely, the cycling performance as shown in Fig. 4b indicated that the NaDFOB-E and NaFSI-E cells were more stable than the $NaPF_{6}-E$ cell, and following $70\ ^{\circ}C$ storage experiment results also confirmed that NaDFOB-E and NaFSI-E cells had better performance than $NaPF_{6}-E$ cell, as shown in Fig. 4c.

source_refs.raw_quote: In this work, we have systemically evaluated and compared the discrepancy of SIBs applying different sodium salts from the view of the salt nature themselves, the properties of corresponding electrolytes, the battery performance and characterization analysis. Although $NaPF_{6}$ has been widely applied in SIBs, NaDFOB and NaFSI should also be paid more attention to broaden their application prospects in SIBs. Thereinto, owing to the limited solubility, single NaDFOB is not suitable for low temperature or high concentration electrolyte. The NaDFOB-E electrolyte enables the cells better performance than $NaPF_{6}-E$ , and is not corrosive to Al foil, indicating NaDFOB is a promising salt choice for room and high temperature electrolyte. Benefit to the superior viscosity, conductivity, and SEI/CEI, the low temperature performance of the cells with NaFSI-E is much better than that of other cells, and after solving the corrosion of NaFSI by additive, NaFSI-E is suitable for low temperature application.

citations.chunk_id: 0017_Fan 等 - 2026 - Difluorophosphate-based electrolyte for pouch sodium-ion batteries with a wide temperature range::sec4::child0
citations.quote: The main raw materials used for preparing functional electrolytes, including ethylene carbonate (EC), ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC), sodium hexafluorophosphate $\left(\mathrm{NaPF}_{6}\right)$ , NaDFP, TMSP and TDFP were provided by the Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. The baseline electrolyte was prepared by dissolving $NaPF_{6}$ in a mixture of EC: EMC = 3:7 to form a concentration of 0.8 mol $L^{-1}$ . Then, 1% (Mass ratio) NaDFP, TDFP, TMSP was added into the baseline electrolyte to prepare corresponding electrolyte. All electrolytes were prepared in a dry argon filled glove box with both moisture and oxygen concentrations below 0.1 ppm. NFM was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co, Ltd., HC was purchased from Kuraray Co Ltd. The pouch test cells with NFM cathode (120 mAh $g^{-1}$ at 0.1C), HC anode (290 mAh $g^{-1}$ at 0.05C), and Celgard 2700 separator were assembled using the conventional assembly method. Thereinto, NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotube (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and Maleic acid were dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) with a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate to prepare the NFM cathode.

citations.chunk_id: 0017_Fan 等 - 2026 - Difluorophosphate-based electrolyte for pouch sodium-ion batteries with a wide temperature range::sec2::child0
citations.quote: Based on the coupling of difluorophosphate-group with -tris(trimethylsilyl)-group of tris(trimethylsilyl)difluorophosphate (TDFP) additive and a “formation-repair” film-forming strategy, a difluorophosphate-based functional electrolyte is developed. This electrolyte facilitates the formation of tough and rich-NaF interfacial films on two electrodes and achieves an enhanced temperature performance of $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) over a wide range from $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . Compared to the cells without TDFP, the capacity retention of pouch NFM/HC cells with TDFP after 400 cycles at $25\ ^{\circ}C$ increases from 0% to 90%, stable cycling performance is obtained after 150 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ , and even the discharge capacity at $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ and the capacity retention after storage at $60\ ^{\circ}C$ are also greatly improved. In addition, the unique properties of TDFP differ from sodium difluorophosphate (NaDFP) and tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphate (TMSP) are analyzed to elucidate the functional mechanisms of TDFP. It is demonstrated that TDFP can not only catalyze the decomposition of $PF_{6}^{-}$ to form NaF-rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI)/cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI) films but also produce $PO_{2}F_{2}^{-}$ to optimize the film composition.

citations.chunk_id: 0017_Fan 等 - 2026 - Difluorophosphate-based electrolyte for pouch sodium-ion batteries with a wide temperature range::sec7::child12
citations.quote: This is likely attributable to the sharp decline in conductivity and the surge in viscosity caused by NaDFP at low temperatures, which weakened the electrolyte's kinetic performance and resulted in inferior rate performance compared to cells with TMSP and TDFP. Furthermore, performance tests were conducted at even lower temperatures, and it was found that the cells with TDFP still maintained an 86% discharge capacity retention rate at -30 °C. Low temperature cycling test is followed to further validate the superior performance of TDFP. As illustrated in Fig. 4d, the cell with TDFP exhibited the best cycling stability, followed by TMSP, then NaDFP, and finally the Baseline. It is worth noting that the performance of TMSP and NaDFP batteries under low-temperature cycling was the reverse of that under room-temperature cycling. This suggests that the failure mechanisms of the batteries and the reasons for performance enhancement by additives also differ. The thicknesses of cells haven't visible change before and after cycling, meaning no significant gas generation could be observed under low-temperature conditions (Fig. 4e). This contrasts with the results under room-temperature cycling, leading to the slightly better performance of TMSP-containing cells compared to NaDFP-containing cells under low-temperature conditions.

citations.chunk_id: 0030_Li 等 - 2025 - An electrolyte design strategy for commercial all-climate pouch sodium-ion batteries::sec7::child13
citations.quote: The illustration of (a) shows a battery powering an LED light to emit light. (c) The cycling performance of pouch NFM/HC cells with 0.3C charge and 0.5C discharge in the range of 1.5–3.8 V at -10 °C. The illustration of (c) shows a model of pouch cell. (d) Low temperature discharge performance at -30°C with different current densities. The cycling performance of pouch NFM/HC cells with/without TMSS at 1C in the range of (e) 1.5–4.0 V at 25 °C and (f) 1.5–3.8 V at 45 °C. It is well established that sodium-ion batteries exhibit superior low-temperature performance compared to lithium-ion batteries. This attribute is of significant potential value for their future applications $[32]$ . Due to the sluggish interfacial kinetics, the energy density and cycle life of SIBs suffer severely at subzero temperatures $[33]$ . Consequently, the electrochemical performance of electrolytes with and without TMSS was evaluated at extreme temperatures. Fig. 3c illustrates that the electrolyte containing TMSS exhibited superior cycling stability and capacity retention compared to the baseline electrolyte at $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ with a 0.3C charge and 0.5C discharge. Batteries without TMSS exhibited a significant decline in capacity, retaining only 60% of their initial capacity after 40 cycles. This was attributed to their low coulombic efficiency and high polarization.

citations.chunk_id: 0030_Li 等 - 2025 - An electrolyte design strategy for commercial all-climate pouch sodium-ion batteries::sec4::child0
citations.quote: Sodium hexafluorophosphate (NaPF $_6$ ), ethylene carbonate (EC) and methyl ethyl carbonate (EMC) were supplied by Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. NaPF $_6$ was dissolved into a EC and EMC (EC: EMC = 3:7 in wt.%) mixture to prepare baseline electrolyte (1 mol/L). Trimethylsilyl methanesulfonate additive (97 %, Shanghai Macklin Biochemical Technology Co., Ltd.) was added into the baseline electrolyte to form functional electrolyte. NFM and HC active materials were purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co., Ltd. and Kuraray Co., Ltd., respectively. The NFM cathode was fabricated from NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotubes (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P) and maleic acid dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) at a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated onto an aluminium substrate. The HC anode was contained 95 % HC, 1.5 % carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), 2.0 % styrene butadiene rubber (SBR), and 1.5 % super P. A Celgard 2700 membrane (Xingyuan Materials Co., Ltd) was as the separator. The mass loading of cathode and anode was 33.0 mg cm $^{-2}$ and 20.1 mg cm $^{-2}$ , respectively. The negative-to-positive (N/P) capacity ratio was 1.1. The empty pouch cells were dried under vacuum at 80 °C for 72 h, then transferred to a glove box and injected 6.0 g electrolyte. Other operations not mentioned were all carried out using the general methods in the battery manufacture.

citations.chunk_id: 0030_Li 等 - 2025 - An electrolyte design strategy for commercial all-climate pouch sodium-ion batteries::sec7
citations.quote:
3.1. Design and performance of the functional electrolyte
To begin with, in order to pre-evaluate the practicability of ether and carbonate ester as the electrolyte in pouch cells, comparative tests were first carried out, as shown in Fig. S1. Although the ether electrolytes have a high initial capacity, their cycling stability is poor, with a capacity retention rate of only 77.38 after 105 cycles, while the carbonate electrolytes have a capacity retention rate of 87.49 %. The gas production behaviour of ether and carbonate ester during long-term cycling at a cut-off voltage of 4.0 V at 45°C was monitored using differential electrochemical mass spectrometry (Fig. S2). It was observed that ether produced a greater quantity of gases, including methane and carbon monoxide, in comparison to carbonate ester. citations.chunk_id: 0030_Li 等 - 2025 - An electrolyte design strategy for commercial all-climate pouch sodium-ion batteries::sec2::child0
citations.quote: A type of wide temperature range electrolyte design strategy incorporating trifunctional trimethylsilyl methanesulfonate (TMSS) additive in specific carbonate ester is developed to enhance the all-climate performance of commercial pouch $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). The incorporation of TMSS serves optimizing the solvation structure to accelerate the reaction kinetics, eliminating residual $H_{2}O/HF$ from the electrolyte, and promoting the formation of high-quality interface films. The capacity retention of the pouch NFM/HC cells with TMSS is effectively enhanced at high-voltage of 4.0 V and wide-temperature range from $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . The cell delivers a high capacity retention of 80 % after 700 cycles at $25\ ^{\circ}C$ , while the initial energy density is as high as 117 Wh kg $^{-1}$ and maintains 103 Wh kg $^{-1}$ after 300 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ and 1C (1C = 900 mA), achieving an 18.2 % increase in energy density. In addition, no obvious gas evolution can be observed when pouch cell is stored at $60\ ^{\circ}C$ and the low-temperature discharge at $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ achieves a 14.76 % increase in capacity at 0.5C. This work demonstrates the feasibility of TMSS in SIBs, and also put insight on the rational electrolyte design of SIBs.

It is well established that sodium-ion batteries exhibit superior low-temperature performance compared to lithium-ion batteries. This attribute is of significant potential value for their future applications $[32]$ . Due to the sluggish interfacial kinetics, the energy density and cycle life of SIBs suffer severely at subzero temperatures $[33]$ . Consequently, the electrochemical performance of electrolytes with and without TMSS was evaluated at extreme temperatures. NaPF $_6$ was dissolved into a EC and EMC (EC: EMC = 3:7 in wt.%) mixture to prepare baseline electrolyte (1 mol/L). The HC anode was contained 95 % HC, 1.5 % carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), 2.0 % styrene butadiene rubber (SBR), and 1.5 % super P. A Celgard 2700 membrane (Xingyuan Materials Co., Ltd) was as the separator. The mass loading of cathode and anode was 33.0 mg cm $^{-2}$ and 20.1 mg cm $^{-2}$ , respectively. The negative-to-positive (N/P) capacity ratio was 1.1. The empty pouch cells were dried under vacuum at 80 °C for 72 h, then transferred to a glove box and injected 6.0 g electrolyte. Other operations not mentioned were all carried out using the general methods in the battery manufacture.

citations.quote: Sodium salts in the electrolytes are key materials for developing high-performance sodium ion batteries (SIBs) due to their direct influences on the electrode reactions and electrolyte conductivity, and sodium fluorophosphate $(\mathrm{NaPF}_6)$ is known to be widely applied. Using $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ as a comparison, this work systematically evaluates the application potential of $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ , sodium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (NaFSI) and sodium difluoro(oxalato)borate (NaDFOB) from the sodium salt nature, electrolyte properties, and battery performance. It is demonstrated that NaFSI can exhibit excellent comprehensive performance and has the potential to substitute for $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ under certain conditions; NaDFOB is more suitable as an additive to improve the high-temperature performance of SIBs. In particular, $\mathrm{NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_2}$ /hard carbon (NFM/HC) SIBs with NaDFOB achieve enhanced performance than that with $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ at high temperature (from $88.2\%$ to $92.4\%$ ), while low temperature performance of NaFSI-containing cells is much better than others (from $0\%$ to $85.9\%$ ).

citations.quote:
3.2. Performance of the batteries with different electrolytes
The effect of sodium salts on the safety is also an important factor for commercial SIBs, and the corrosion of battery devices is one of the reference bases for sodium salt selection. Fig. 3e and f shows the corrosion results of Al foil in different electrolytes. As is reported at previous research, NaFSI-E would corrode Al foil during cycling so that may cause safety issues where NaDFOB-E and $\mathrm{NaPF_6 - E}$ hardly react. The coin cell was used to evaluate the corrosion of Al foil in different electrolytes. Surprisingly, although it can still observe obvious corrosion products on the glass fiber after cycling with NaFSI-E when measured with the coin cell, the Al foil inside the SIBs remains integrity, but the battery shell has obvious corrosion traces, as shown in Fig. 3g, which is quite different from the result measured by the electrolytic tank as shown in Fig. 3h. From this phenomenon, it can be inferred that NaFSI-E would corrode Al foil as well as stainless steel but corrode stainless steel first.

Battery performance is the most straightly and convincing evidence to evaluate the electrolytes with different sodium salts. At present stage, NFM and HC are widely considered as ideal cathode and anode materials for commercial pouch SIBs due to their duration to water and air $[23–26]$ . The electrochemical performance of NFM||HC pouch SIBs with various electrolytes including $NaPF_{6}$ , NaFSI and NaDFOB from $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ to $70\ ^{\circ}C$ , have been thoroughly investigated. The rate capability of the cells with different electrolytes at various current densities under $45\ ^{\circ}C$ was firstly studied, as illustrated in Fig. 4a. The $NaPF_{6}-E$ and NaFSI-E cells showed similar rate capabilities, while the NaDFOB-E cell exhibited inferior performance. Conversely, the cycling performance as shown in Fig. 4b indicated that the NaDFOB-E and NaFSI-E cells were more stable than the $NaPF_{6}-E$ cell, and following $70\ ^{\circ}C$ storage experiment results also confirmed that NaDFOB-E and NaFSI-E cells had better performance than $NaPF_{6}-E$ cell, as shown in Fig. 4c.

citations.quote: In this work, we have systemically evaluated and compared the discrepancy of SIBs applying different sodium salts from the view of the salt nature themselves, the properties of corresponding electrolytes, the battery performance and characterization analysis. Although $NaPF_{6}$ has been widely applied in SIBs, NaDFOB and NaFSI should also be paid more attention to broaden their application prospects in SIBs. Thereinto, owing to the limited solubility, single NaDFOB is not suitable for low temperature or high concentration electrolyte. The NaDFOB-E electrolyte enables the cells better performance than $NaPF_{6}-E$ , and is not corrosive to Al foil, indicating NaDFOB is a promising salt choice for room and high temperature electrolyte. Benefit to the superior viscosity, conductivity, and SEI/CEI, the low temperature performance of the cells with NaFSI-E is much better than that of other cells, and after solving the corrosion of NaFSI by additive, NaFSI-E is suitable for low temperature application.

evidence_ledger.quote: Sodium hexafluorophosphate (NaPF $_6$ ), ethylene carbonate (EC) and methyl ethyl carbonate (EMC) were supplied by Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. NaPF $_6$ was dissolved into a EC and EMC (EC: EMC = 3:7 in wt.%) mixture to prepare baseline electrolyte (1 mol/L). Trimethylsilyl methanesulfonate additive (97 %, Shanghai Macklin Biochemical Technology Co., Ltd.) was added into the baseline electrolyte to form functional electrolyte. NFM and HC active materials were purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co., Ltd. and Kuraray Co., Ltd., respectively. The NFM cathode was fabricated from NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotubes (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P) and maleic acid dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) at a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated onto an aluminium substrate. The HC anode was contained 95 % HC, 1.5 % carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), 2.0 % styrene butadiene rubber (SBR), and 1.5 % super P. A Celgard 2700 membrane (Xingyuan Materials Co., Ltd) was as the separator. The mass loading of cathode and anode was 33.0 mg cm $^{-2}$ and 20.1 mg cm $^{-2}$ , respectively. The negative-to-positive (N/P) capacity ratio was 1.1. The empty pouch cells were dried under vacuum at 80 °C for 72 h, then transferred to a glove box and injected 6.0 g electrolyte. Other operations not mentioned were all carried out using the general methods in the battery manufacture.

evidence_ledger.quote:
3.1. Design and performance of the functional electrolyte
To begin with, in order to pre-evaluate the practicability of ether and carbonate ester as the electrolyte in pouch cells, comparative tests were first carried out, as shown in Fig. S1. Although the ether electrolytes have a high initial capacity, their cycling stability is poor, with a capacity retention rate of only 77.38 after 105 cycles, while the carbonate electrolytes have a capacity retention rate of 87.49 %. The gas production behaviour of ether and carbonate ester during long-term cycling at a cut-off voltage of 4.0 V at 45°C was monitored using differential electrochemical mass spectrometry (Fig. S2). It was observed that ether produced a greater quantity of gases, including methane and carbon monoxide, in comparison to carbonate ester. This may be a contributing factor to the unsuitability of ether for use in pouch cells, due to the rapid consumption of electrolyte, which results in a rapid decline in battery capacity. The electrolyte formula employs a combination of 1 mol/L NaPF $_{6}$ , cyclic ester EC and linear ester EMC in a mass ratio of 3:7 (called Baseline electrolyte), augmented by the incorporation of 3 wt% TMSS as a functional additive. The introduction of linear esters engenders a reduction in viscosity and an enhanced capacity to dissolve sodium salts in the electrolyte as a whole, thereby facilitating an improvement in the fluidity and ion conductivity of the electrolyte. Compounds containing sulfone groups, such as 1,3-propanesultone (PS), have been demonstrated to have excellent effects in inhibiting gas production and improving high-temperature performance (Fig. 1a). Consequently, they have been introduced into electrolytes and have become widely used. Compounds containing siloxane structures, such as trimethylsilyl isocyanate, exhibit high reactivity due to the facile rupture of their Si-O bonds. This enables effective removal of moisture and acid from the electrolyte and protection of the electrode electrolyte interface phase [25,26]. Therefore, the incorporation of TMSS is anticipated to combine the aforementioned effects with functional electrolytes, thereby achieving high-performance NFM/HC SIBs.

It is well established that sodium-ion batteries exhibit superior low-temperature performance compared to lithium-ion batteries. This attribute is of significant potential value for their future applications $[32]$ . Due to the sluggish interfacial kinetics, the energy density and cycle life of SIBs suffer severely at subzero temperatures $[33]$ . Consequently, the electrochemical performance of electrolytes with and without TMSS was evaluated at extreme temperatures. Fig. 3c illustrates that the electrolyte containing TMSS exhibited superior cycling stability and capacity retention compared to the baseline electrolyte at $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ with a 0.3C charge and 0.5C discharge. Batteries without TMSS exhibited a significant decline in capacity, retaining only 60% of their initial capacity after 40 cycles. This was attributed to their low coulombic efficiency and high polarization.

evidence_ledger.chunk_id: 0030_Li 等 - 2025 - An electrolyte design strategy for commercial all-climate pouch sodium-ion batteries::sec2::child0
evidence_ledger.paper_id: 0030_Li 等 - 2025 - An electrolyte design strategy for commercial all-climate pouch sodium-ion batteries
evidence_ledger.quote: A type of wide temperature range electrolyte design strategy incorporating trifunctional trimethylsilyl methanesulfonate (TMSS) additive in specific carbonate ester is developed to enhance the all-climate performance of commercial pouch $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). The incorporation of TMSS serves optimizing the solvation structure to accelerate the reaction kinetics, eliminating residual $H_{2}O/HF$ from the electrolyte, and promoting the formation of high-quality interface films. The capacity retention of the pouch NFM/HC cells with TMSS is effectively enhanced at high-voltage of 4.0 V and wide-temperature range from $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . The cell delivers a high capacity retention of 80 % after 700 cycles at $25\ ^{\circ}C$ , while the initial energy density is as high as 117 Wh kg $^{-1}$ and maintains 103 Wh kg $^{-1}$ after 300 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ and 1C (1C = 900 mA), achieving an 18.2 % increase in energy density. In addition, no obvious gas evolution can be observed when pouch cell is stored at $60\ ^{\circ}C$ and the low-temperature discharge at $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ achieves a 14.76 % increase in capacity at 0.5C. This work demonstrates the feasibility of TMSS in SIBs, and also put insight on the rational electrolyte design of SIBs.

evidence_ledger.quote: Based on the coupling of difluorophosphate-group with -tris(trimethylsilyl)-group of tris(trimethylsilyl)difluorophosphate (TDFP) additive and a “formation-repair” film-forming strategy, a difluorophosphate-based functional electrolyte is developed. This electrolyte facilitates the formation of tough and rich-NaF interfacial films on two electrodes and achieves an enhanced temperature performance of $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) over a wide range from $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . Compared to the cells without TDFP, the capacity retention of pouch NFM/HC cells with TDFP after 400 cycles at $25\ ^{\circ}C$ increases from 0% to 90%, stable cycling performance is obtained after 150 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ , and even the discharge capacity at $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ and the capacity retention after storage at $60\ ^{\circ}C$ are also greatly improved. In addition, the unique properties of TDFP differ from sodium difluorophosphate (NaDFP) and tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphate (TMSP) are analyzed to elucidate the functional mechanisms of TDFP. It is demonstrated that TDFP can not only catalyze the decomposition of $PF_{6}^{-}$ to form NaF-rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI)/cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI) films but also produce $PO_{2}F_{2}^{-}$ to optimize the film composition.

evidence_ledger.quote: This allows it to maintain good performance in low temperature conditions. During the charge and discharge process, TMSS is capable of capturing the HF generated by the hydrolysis of $PF_{6}^{-}$ in the solvent due to the presence of trace amounts of water. This protects the positive electrode material from corrosion and reduces the dissolution of transition metal ions. Additionally, the S = O group of the abundant charge carrier can stabilize $PF_{5}$ , reduce the opening of the solvent EC, and thus reduce the gas production of the pouch cells. This ensures that the battery will remain in good working order under conditions of high temperature. Moreover, TMSS exhibits a preferential oxidation and decomposition process, resulting in the formation of low impedance, high ion mobility CEI films and SEI films rich in S-based and Si-based compounds on the cathode and anode surfaces. These films have the capacity to inhibit the decomposition of $PF_{6}$ and improve the thermodynamic and kinetic stability of the electrolyte.

evidence_ledger.quote: Sodium salts in the electrolytes are key materials for developing high-performance sodium ion batteries (SIBs) due to their direct influences on the electrode reactions and electrolyte conductivity, and sodium fluorophosphate $(\mathrm{NaPF}_6)$ is known to be widely applied. Using $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ as a comparison, this work systematically evaluates the application potential of $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ , sodium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (NaFSI) and sodium difluoro(oxalato)borate (NaDFOB) from the sodium salt nature, electrolyte properties, and battery performance. It is demonstrated that NaFSI can exhibit excellent comprehensive performance and has the potential to substitute for $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ under certain conditions; NaDFOB is more suitable as an additive to improve the high-temperature performance of SIBs. In particular, $\mathrm{NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_2}$ /hard carbon (NFM/HC) SIBs with NaDFOB achieve enhanced performance than that with $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ at high temperature (from $88.2\%$ to $92.4\%$ ), while low temperature performance of NaFSI-containing cells is much better than others (from $0\%$ to $85.9\%$ ).

evidence_ledger.quote:
3.2. Performance of the batteries with different electrolytes
The effect of sodium salts on the safety is also an important factor for commercial SIBs, and the corrosion of battery devices is one of the reference bases for sodium salt selection. Fig. 3e and f shows the corrosion results of Al foil in different electrolytes. As is reported at previous research, NaFSI-E would corrode Al foil during cycling so that may cause safety issues where NaDFOB-E and $\mathrm{NaPF_6 - E}$ hardly react. The coin cell was used to evaluate the corrosion of Al foil in different electrolytes. Surprisingly, although it can still observe obvious corrosion products on the glass fiber after cycling with NaFSI-E when measured with the coin cell, the Al foil inside the SIBs remains integrity, but the battery shell has obvious corrosion traces, as shown in Fig. 3g, which is quite different from the result measured by the electrolytic tank as shown in Fig. 3h. From this phenomenon, it can be inferred that NaFSI-E would corrode Al foil as well as stainless steel but corrode stainless steel first.

Battery performance is the most straightly and convincing evidence to evaluate the electrolytes with different sodium salts. At present stage, NFM and HC are widely considered as ideal cathode and anode materials for commercial pouch SIBs due to their duration to water and air $[23–26]$ . The electrochemical performance of NFM||HC pouch SIBs with various electrolytes including $NaPF_{6}$ , NaFSI and NaDFOB from $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ to $70\ ^{\circ}C$ , have been thoroughly investigated. The rate capability of the cells with different electrolytes at various current densities under $45\ ^{\circ}C$ was firstly studied, as illustrated in Fig. 4a. The $NaPF_{6}-E$ and NaFSI-E cells showed similar rate capabilities, while the NaDFOB-E cell exhibited inferior performance. Conversely, the cycling performance as shown in Fig. 4b indicated that the NaDFOB-E and NaFSI-E cells were more stable than the $NaPF_{6}-E$ cell, and following $70\ ^{\circ}C$ storage experiment results also confirmed that NaDFOB-E and NaFSI-E cells had better performance than $NaPF_{6}-E$ cell, as shown in Fig. 4c.

evidence_ledger.quote: In this work, we have systemically evaluated and compared the discrepancy of SIBs applying different sodium salts from the view of the salt nature themselves, the properties of corresponding electrolytes, the battery performance and characterization analysis. Although $NaPF_{6}$ has been widely applied in SIBs, NaDFOB and NaFSI should also be paid more attention to broaden their application prospects in SIBs. Thereinto, owing to the limited solubility, single NaDFOB is not suitable for low temperature or high concentration electrolyte. The NaDFOB-E electrolyte enables the cells better performance than $NaPF_{6}-E$ , and is not corrosive to Al foil, indicating NaDFOB is a promising salt choice for room and high temperature electrolyte. Benefit to the superior viscosity, conductivity, and SEI/CEI, the low temperature performance of the cells with NaFSI-E is much better than that of other cells, and after solving the corrosion of NaFSI by additive, NaFSI-E is suitable for low temperature application.

citations.chunk_id: 0017_Fan 等 - 2026 - Difluorophosphate-based electrolyte for pouch sodium-ion batteries with a wide temperature range::sec4::child0
citations.quote: The main raw materials used for preparing functional electrolytes, including ethylene carbonate (EC), ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC), sodium hexafluorophosphate $\left(\mathrm{NaPF}_{6}\right)$ , NaDFP, TMSP and TDFP were provided by the Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. The baseline electrolyte was prepared by dissolving $NaPF_{6}$ in a mixture of EC: EMC = 3:7 to form a concentration of 0.8 mol $L^{-1}$ . Then, 1% (Mass ratio) NaDFP, TDFP, TMSP was added into the baseline electrolyte to prepare corresponding electrolyte. All electrolytes were prepared in a dry argon filled glove box with both moisture and oxygen concentrations below 0.1 ppm. NFM was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co, Ltd., HC was purchased from Kuraray Co Ltd. The pouch test cells with NFM cathode (120 mAh $g^{-1}$ at 0.1C), HC anode (290 mAh $g^{-1}$ at 0.05C), and Celgard 2700 separator were assembled using the conventional assembly method. Thereinto, NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotube (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and Maleic acid were dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) with a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate to prepare the NFM cathode.

citations.chunk_id: 0017_Fan 等 - 2026 - Difluorophosphate-based electrolyte for pouch sodium-ion batteries with a wide temperature range::sec2::child0
citations.quote: Based on the coupling of difluorophosphate-group with -tris(trimethylsilyl)-group of tris(trimethylsilyl)difluorophosphate (TDFP) additive and a “formation-repair” film-forming strategy, a difluorophosphate-based functional electrolyte is developed. This electrolyte facilitates the formation of tough and rich-NaF interfacial films on two electrodes and achieves an enhanced temperature performance of $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) over a wide range from $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . Compared to the cells without TDFP, the capacity retention of pouch NFM/HC cells with TDFP after 400 cycles at $25\ ^{\circ}C$ increases from 0% to 90%, stable cycling performance is obtained after 150 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ , and even the discharge capacity at $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ and the capacity retention after storage at $60\ ^{\circ}C$ are also greatly improved. In addition, the unique properties of TDFP differ from sodium difluorophosphate (NaDFP) and tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphate (TMSP) are analyzed to elucidate the functional mechanisms of TDFP. It is demonstrated that TDFP can not only catalyze the decomposition of $PF_{6}^{-}$ to form NaF-rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI)/cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI) films but also produce $PO_{2}F_{2}^{-}$ to optimize the film composition.

citations.quote: This is likely attributable to the sharp decline in conductivity and the surge in viscosity caused by NaDFP at low temperatures, which weakened the electrolyte's kinetic performance and resulted in inferior rate performance compared to cells with TMSP and TDFP. Furthermore, performance tests were conducted at even lower temperatures, and it was found that the cells with TDFP still maintained an 86% discharge capacity retention rate at -30 °C. Low temperature cycling test is followed to further validate the superior performance of TDFP. As illustrated in Fig. 4d, the cell with TDFP exhibited the best cycling stability, followed by TMSP, then NaDFP, and finally the Baseline. It is worth noting that the performance of TMSP and NaDFP batteries under low-temperature cycling was the reverse of that under room-temperature cycling. This suggests that the failure mechanisms of the batteries and the reasons for performance enhancement by additives also differ. The thicknesses of cells haven't visible change before and after cycling, meaning no significant gas generation could be observed under low-temperature conditions (Fig. 4e). This contrasts with the results under room-temperature cycling, leading to the slightly better performance of TMSP-containing cells compared to NaDFP-containing cells under low-temperature conditions.

It is well established that sodium-ion batteries exhibit superior low-temperature performance compared to lithium-ion batteries. This attribute is of significant potential value for their future applications $[32]$ . Due to the sluggish interfacial kinetics, the energy density and cycle life of SIBs suffer severely at subzero temperatures $[33]$ . citations.quote: Sodium hexafluorophosphate (NaPF $_6$ ), ethylene carbonate (EC) and methyl ethyl carbonate (EMC) were supplied by Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. NaPF $_6$ was dissolved into a EC and EMC (EC: EMC = 3:7 in wt.%) mixture to prepare baseline electrolyte (1 mol/L). Trimethylsilyl methanesulfonate additive (97 %, Shanghai Macklin Biochemical Technology Co., Ltd.) was added into the baseline electrolyte to form functional electrolyte. NFM and HC active materials were purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co., Ltd. and Kuraray Co., Ltd., respectively. The NFM cathode was fabricated from NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotubes (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P) and maleic acid dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) at a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated onto an aluminium substrate. The HC anode was contained 95 % HC, 1.5 % carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), 2.0 % styrene butadiene rubber (SBR), and 1.5 % super P. A Celgard 2700 membrane (Xingyuan Materials Co., Ltd) was as the separator. The mass loading of cathode and anode was 33.0 mg cm $^{-2}$ and 20.1 mg cm $^{-2}$ , respectively. The negative-to-positive (N/P) capacity ratio was 1.1. The empty pouch cells were dried under vacuum at 80 °C for 72 h, then transferred to a glove box and injected 6.0 g electrolyte. Other operations not mentioned were all carried out using the general methods in the battery manufacture.

citations.quote:
3.1. Design and performance of the functional electrolyte
To begin with, in order to pre-evaluate the practicability of ether and carbonate ester as the electrolyte in pouch cells, comparative tests were first carried out, as shown in Fig. S1. Although the ether electrolytes have a high initial capacity, their cycling stability is poor, with a capacity retention rate of only 77.38 after 105 cycles, while the carbonate electrolytes have a capacity retention rate of 87.49 %. The gas production behaviour of ether and carbonate ester during long-term cycling at a cut-off voltage of 4.0 V at 45°C was monitored using differential electrochemical mass spectrometry (Fig. S2). It was observed that ether produced a greater quantity of gases, including methane and carbon monoxide, in comparison to carbonate ester. This may be a contributing factor to the unsuitability of ether for use in pouch cells, due to the rapid consumption of electrolyte, which results in a rapid decline in battery capacity. The electrolyte formula employs a combination of 1 mol/L NaPF $_{6}$ , cyclic ester EC and linear ester EMC in a mass ratio of 3:7 (called Baseline electrolyte), augmented by the incorporation of 3 wt% TMSS as a functional additive. The introduction of linear esters engenders a reduction in viscosity and an enhanced capacity to dissolve sodium salts in the electrolyte as a whole, thereby facilitating an improvement in the fluidity and ion conductivity of the electrolyte. Compounds containing sulfone groups, such as 1,3-propanesultone (PS), have been demonstrated to have excellent effects in inhibiting gas production and improving high-temperature performance (Fig. 1a). Consequently, they have been introduced into electrolytes and have become widely used. Compounds containing siloxane structures, such as trimethylsilyl isocyanate, exhibit high reactivity due to the facile rupture of their Si-O bonds. This enables effective removal of moisture and acid from the electrolyte and protection of the electrode electrolyte interface phase [25,26]. Therefore, the incorporation of TMSS is anticipated to combine the aforementioned effects with functional electrolytes, thereby achieving high-performance NFM/HC SIBs.

citations.chunk_id: 0030_Li 等 - 2025 - An electrolyte design strategy for commercial all-climate pouch sodium-ion batteries::sec2::child0
citations.quote: A type of wide temperature range electrolyte design strategy incorporating trifunctional trimethylsilyl methanesulfonate (TMSS) additive in specific carbonate ester is developed to enhance the all-climate performance of commercial pouch $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). The incorporation of TMSS serves optimizing the solvation structure to accelerate the reaction kinetics, eliminating residual $H_{2}O/HF$ from the electrolyte, and promoting the formation of high-quality interface films. The capacity retention of the pouch NFM/HC cells with TMSS is effectively enhanced at high-voltage of 4.0 V and wide-temperature range from $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . The cell delivers a high capacity retention of 80 % after 700 cycles at $25\ ^{\circ}C$ , while the initial energy density is as high as 117 Wh kg $^{-1}$ and maintains 103 Wh kg $^{-1}$ after 300 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ and 1C (1C = 900 mA), achieving an 18.2 % increase in energy density. In addition, no obvious gas evolution can be observed when pouch cell is stored at $60\ ^{\circ}C$ and the low-temperature discharge at $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ achieves a 14.76 % increase in capacity at 0.5C. This work demonstrates the feasibility of TMSS in SIBs, and also put insight on the rational electrolyte design of SIBs.

citations.quote: Sodium salts in the electrolytes are key materials for developing high-performance sodium ion batteries (SIBs) due to their direct influences on the electrode reactions and electrolyte conductivity, and sodium fluorophosphate $(\mathrm{NaPF}_6)$ is known to be widely applied. Using $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ as a comparison, this work systematically evaluates the application potential of $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ , sodium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (NaFSI) and sodium difluoro(oxalato)borate (NaDFOB) from the sodium salt nature, electrolyte properties, and battery performance. It is demonstrated that NaFSI can exhibit excellent comprehensive performance and has the potential to substitute for $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ under certain conditions; NaDFOB is more suitable as an additive to improve the high-temperature performance of SIBs. In particular, $\mathrm{NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_2}$ /hard carbon (NFM/HC) SIBs with NaDFOB achieve enhanced performance than that with $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ at high temperature (from $88.2\%$ to $92.4\%$ ), while low temperature performance of NaFSI-containing cells is much better than others (from $0\%$ to $85.9\%$ ).

The solubility of three salts at different temperatures in the commonly used commercial solvent combinations (EC/EMC = 1:1) was tested. It was indicated that the solubility of NaDFOB was significantly lower than that of the other two salts, as shown in Fig. 1c and Fig. S1, indicating NaDFOB might not be suitable for high concentration or low temperature electrolyte as a main salt. Thus, the 0.8 M electrolytes containing different sodium salts were further investigated. The LSV curves of the electrolytes in the voltage range of 2.0–5.5 V (vs. Na/Na $^{+}$ ) were used to evaluate the electrochemical stable window (ESW) of electrolytes. As shown in Fig. 1d, no obvious oxidation current peaks were observed in NaPF $_{6}$ -E and NaDFOB-E below 4.5 V. The density of three electrolytes (0.8 M) is shown in Fig. 1e, where injection amount of NaFSI-E might much more than other. 3.2. Performance of the batteries with different electrolytes
The effect of sodium salts on the safety is also an important factor for commercial SIBs, and the corrosion of battery devices is one of the reference bases for sodium salt selection. Fig. 3e and f shows the corrosion results of Al foil in different electrolytes. As is reported at previous research, NaFSI-E would corrode Al foil during cycling so that may cause safety issues where NaDFOB-E and $\mathrm{NaPF_6 - E}$ hardly react. The coin cell was used to evaluate the corrosion of Al foil in different electrolytes. Surprisingly, although it can still observe obvious corrosion products on the glass fiber after cycling with NaFSI-E when measured with the coin cell, the Al foil inside the SIBs remains integrity, but the battery shell has obvious corrosion traces, as shown in Fig. 3g, which is quite different from the result measured by the electrolytic tank as shown in Fig. 3h. From this phenomenon, it can be inferred that NaFSI-E would corrode Al foil as well as stainless steel but corrode stainless steel first.

Battery performance is the most straightly and convincing evidence to evaluate the electrolytes with different sodium salts. At present stage, NFM and HC are widely considered as ideal cathode and anode materials for commercial pouch SIBs due to their duration to water and air $[23–26]$ . The electrochemical performance of NFM||HC pouch SIBs with various electrolytes including $NaPF_{6}$ , NaFSI and NaDFOB from $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ to $70\ ^{\circ}C$ , have been thoroughly investigated. The rate capability of the cells with different electrolytes at various current densities under $45\ ^{\circ}C$ was firstly studied, as illustrated in Fig. 4a. The $NaPF_{6}-E$ and NaFSI-E cells showed similar rate capabilities, while the NaDFOB-E cell exhibited inferior performance. Conversely, the cycling performance as shown in Fig. 4b indicated that the NaDFOB-E and NaFSI-E cells were more stable than the $NaPF_{6}-E$ cell, and following $70\ ^{\circ}C$ storage experiment results also confirmed that NaDFOB-E and NaFSI-E cells had better performance than $NaPF_{6}-E$ cell, as shown in Fig. 4c.

Although $NaPF_{6}$ has been widely applied in SIBs, NaDFOB and NaFSI should also be paid more attention to broaden their application prospects in SIBs. Thereinto, owing to the limited solubility, single NaDFOB is not suitable for low temperature or high concentration electrolyte. The NaDFOB-E electrolyte enables the cells better performance than $NaPF_{6}-E$ , and is not corrosive to Al foil, indicating NaDFOB is a promising salt choice for room and high temperature electrolyte. Benefit to the superior viscosity, conductivity, and SEI/CEI, the low temperature performance of the cells with NaFSI-E is much better than that of other cells, and after solving the corrosion of NaFSI by additive, NaFSI-E is suitable for low temperature application.

citations.chunk_id: 0017_Fan 等 - 2026 - Difluorophosphate-based electrolyte for pouch sodium-ion batteries with a wide temperature range::sec2::child0
citations.quote: Based on the coupling of difluorophosphate-group with -tris(trimethylsilyl)-group of tris(trimethylsilyl)difluorophosphate (TDFP) additive and a “formation-repair” film-forming strategy, a difluorophosphate-based functional electrolyte is developed. This electrolyte facilitates the formation of tough and rich-NaF interfacial films on two electrodes and achieves an enhanced temperature performance of $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) over a wide range from $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . Compared to the cells without TDFP, the capacity retention of pouch NFM/HC cells with TDFP after 400 cycles at $25\ ^{\circ}C$ increases from 0% to 90%, stable cycling performance is obtained after 150 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ , and even the discharge capacity at $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ and the capacity retention after storage at $60\ ^{\circ}C$ are also greatly improved. In addition, the unique properties of TDFP differ from sodium difluorophosphate (NaDFP) and tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphate (TMSP) are analyzed to elucidate the functional mechanisms of TDFP. It is demonstrated that TDFP can not only catalyze the decomposition of $PF_{6}^{-}$ to form NaF-rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI)/cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI) films but also produce $PO_{2}F_{2}^{-}$ to optimize the film composition.

As illustrated in Fig. 4d, the cell with TDFP exhibited the best cycling stability, followed by TMSP, then NaDFP, and finally the Baseline. association_citations.chunk_id: 0017_Fan 等 - 2026 - Difluorophosphate-based electrolyte for pouch sodium-ion batteries with a wide temperature range::sec2::child0
association_citations.quote: Based on the coupling of difluorophosphate-group with -tris(trimethylsilyl)-group of tris(trimethylsilyl)difluorophosphate (TDFP) additive and a “formation-repair” film-forming strategy, a difluorophosphate-based functional electrolyte is developed. This electrolyte facilitates the formation of tough and rich-NaF interfacial films on two electrodes and achieves an enhanced temperature performance of $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) over a wide range from $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . Compared to the cells without TDFP, the capacity retention of pouch NFM/HC cells with TDFP after 400 cycles at $25\ ^{\circ}C$ increases from 0% to 90%, stable cycling performance is obtained after 150 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ , and even the discharge capacity at $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ and the capacity retention after storage at $60\ ^{\circ}C$ are also greatly improved. In addition, the unique properties of TDFP differ from sodium difluorophosphate (NaDFP) and tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphate (TMSP) are analyzed to elucidate the functional mechanisms of TDFP. It is demonstrated that TDFP can not only catalyze the decomposition of $PF_{6}^{-}$ to form NaF-rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI)/cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI) films but also produce $PO_{2}F_{2}^{-}$ to optimize the film composition.

citations.quote:
3.1. Design and performance of the functional electrolyte
To begin with, in order to pre-evaluate the practicability of ether and carbonate ester as the electrolyte in pouch cells, comparative tests were first carried out, as shown in Fig. S1. Although the ether electrolytes have a high initial capacity, their cycling stability is poor, with a capacity retention rate of only 77.38 after 105 cycles, while the carbonate electrolytes have a capacity retention rate of 87.49 %. The gas production behaviour of ether and carbonate ester during long-term cycling at a cut-off voltage of 4.0 V at 45°C was monitored using differential electrochemical mass spectrometry (Fig. S2). It was observed that ether produced a greater quantity of gases, including methane and carbon monoxide, in comparison to carbonate ester. This may be a contributing factor to the unsuitability of ether for use in pouch cells, due to the rapid consumption of electrolyte, which results in a rapid decline in battery capacity. The electrolyte formula employs a combination of 1 mol/L NaPF $_{6}$ , cyclic ester EC and linear ester EMC in a mass ratio of 3:7 (called Baseline electrolyte), augmented by the incorporation of 3 wt% TMSS as a functional additive. The introduction of linear esters engenders a reduction in viscosity and an enhanced capacity to dissolve sodium salts in the electrolyte as a whole, thereby facilitating an improvement in the fluidity and ion conductivity of the electrolyte. Compounds containing sulfone groups, such as 1,3-propanesultone (PS), have been demonstrated to have excellent effects in inhibiting gas production and improving high-temperature performance (Fig. 1a). Consequently, they have been introduced into electrolytes and have become widely used. Compounds containing siloxane structures, such as trimethylsilyl isocyanate, exhibit high reactivity due to the facile rupture of their Si-O bonds. This enables effective removal of moisture and acid from the electrolyte and protection of the electrode electrolyte interface phase [25,26]. Therefore, the incorporation of TMSS is anticipated to combine the aforementioned effects with functional electrolytes, thereby achieving high-performance NFM/HC SIBs.

citations.chunk_id: 0030_Li 等 - 2025 - An electrolyte design strategy for commercial all-climate pouch sodium-ion batteries::sec2::child0
citations.quote: A type of wide temperature range electrolyte design strategy incorporating trifunctional trimethylsilyl methanesulfonate (TMSS) additive in specific carbonate ester is developed to enhance the all-climate performance of commercial pouch $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). The incorporation of TMSS serves optimizing the solvation structure to accelerate the reaction kinetics, eliminating residual $H_{2}O/HF$ from the electrolyte, and promoting the formation of high-quality interface films. The capacity retention of the pouch NFM/HC cells with TMSS is effectively enhanced at high-voltage of 4.0 V and wide-temperature range from $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . The cell delivers a high capacity retention of 80 % after 700 cycles at $25\ ^{\circ}C$ , while the initial energy density is as high as 117 Wh kg $^{-1}$ and maintains 103 Wh kg $^{-1}$ after 300 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ and 1C (1C = 900 mA), achieving an 18.2 % increase in energy density. In addition, no obvious gas evolution can be observed when pouch cell is stored at $60\ ^{\circ}C$ and the low-temperature discharge at $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ achieves a 14.76 % increase in capacity at 0.5C. This work demonstrates the feasibility of TMSS in SIBs, and also put insight on the rational electrolyte design of SIBs.

citations.quote: This allows it to maintain good performance in low temperature conditions. During the charge and discharge process, TMSS is capable of capturing the HF generated by the hydrolysis of $PF_{6}^{-}$ in the solvent due to the presence of trace amounts of water. This protects the positive electrode material from corrosion and reduces the dissolution of transition metal ions. Additionally, the S = O group of the abundant charge carrier can stabilize $PF_{5}$ , reduce the opening of the solvent EC, and thus reduce the gas production of the pouch cells. This ensures that the battery will remain in good working order under conditions of high temperature. Moreover, TMSS exhibits a preferential oxidation and decomposition process, resulting in the formation of low impedance, high ion mobility CEI films and SEI films rich in S-based and Si-based compounds on the cathode and anode surfaces. These films have the capacity to inhibit the decomposition of $PF_{6}$ and improve the thermodynamic and kinetic stability of the electrolyte.

citations.quote: Taking into account the application environment temperature and corresponding performance requirements of the SIBs, the performance parameters of pouch cells under different temperature conditions after adding different electrolytes were evaluated in a targeted manner. In order to choose the optimal concentration, part of the tough condition performance corresponding to different addition amounts of two additives is shown in Fig. S3. Considering cost and performance comprehensively, a 1:1.5 proportioning of NaDFP to TMSB or TMSB is chosen as the most suitable ratio. First, under the room and high temperatures, the emphasis of pouch cells with different electrolytes was given to the rate, cycling and storage performance parameters. The pouch cells with NB, NP, or NaDFP-containing electrolytes generally exhibit higher performance parameters than the cells with the baseline electrolyte. Under the room temperature of 25 °C, as shown in the Fig. S4a and S4b, rate and cycling performance of the pouch cells with the NB and NP-containing electrolytes is improved comparing to the cells with the baseline electrolyte, which can easily ascribed to the superior conductivity and lower desolvation energy. To further verify the effect of NP, NB, and NaDFP electrolytes at tougher conditions, rate, cycling, and storage tests at 45 °C and 60 °C were performed.

citations.quote: Sodium salts in the electrolytes are key materials for developing high-performance sodium ion batteries (SIBs) due to their direct influences on the electrode reactions and electrolyte conductivity, and sodium fluorophosphate $(\mathrm{NaPF}_6)$ is known to be widely applied. Using $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ as a comparison, this work systematically evaluates the application potential of $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ , sodium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (NaFSI) and sodium difluoro(oxalato)borate (NaDFOB) from the sodium salt nature, electrolyte properties, and battery performance. It is demonstrated that NaFSI can exhibit excellent comprehensive performance and has the potential to substitute for $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ under certain conditions; NaDFOB is more suitable as an additive to improve the high-temperature performance of SIBs. In particular, $\mathrm{NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_2}$ /hard carbon (NFM/HC) SIBs with NaDFOB achieve enhanced performance than that with $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ at high temperature (from $88.2\%$ to $92.4\%$ ), while low temperature performance of NaFSI-containing cells is much better than others (from $0\%$ to $85.9\%$ ).

citations.quote: Besides, the physicochemical properties of three electrolytes containing NaDFOB (NaDFOB-E), $NaPF_{6}$ ( $NaPF_{6}-E$ ), and NaFSI (NaFSI-E) were measured. The solubility of three salts at different temperatures in the commonly used commercial solvent combinations (EC/EMC = 1:1) was tested. It was indicated that the solubility of NaDFOB was significantly lower than that of the other two salts, as shown in Fig. 1c and Fig. S1, indicating NaDFOB might not be suitable for high concentration or low temperature electrolyte as a main salt. Thus, the 0.8 M electrolytes containing different sodium salts were further investigated. The LSV curves of the electrolytes in the voltage range of 2.0–5.5 V (vs. Na/Na $^{+}$ ) were used to evaluate the electrochemical stable window (ESW) of electrolytes. As shown in Fig. 1d, no obvious oxidation current peaks were observed in NaPF $_{6}$ -E and NaDFOB-E below 4.5 V. The oxidation current peak of NaFSI-E increased far more sharply when the voltage exceeded 4.0 V, which might be attributed to the instability of FSI $^{-}$ anions under higher voltage. The density of three electrolytes (0.8 M) is shown in Fig. 1e, where injection amount of NaFSI-E might much more than other. In addition, the viscosity and conductivity are also important properties for commercial electrolyte, which deeply affects the performance of SIBs, especially at the low temperature.
