citations.quote:
3.2. Performance of the batteries with different electrolytes
The effect of sodium salts on the safety is also an important factor for commercial SIBs, and the corrosion of battery devices is one of the reference bases for sodium salt selection. Fig. 3e and f shows the corrosion results of Al foil in different electrolytes. As is reported at previous research, NaFSI-E would corrode Al foil during cycling so that may cause safety issues where NaDFOB-E and $\mathrm{NaPF_6 - E}$ hardly react. The coin cell was used to evaluate the corrosion of Al foil in different electrolytes. Surprisingly, although it can still observe obvious corrosion products on the glass fiber after cycling with NaFSI-E when measured with the coin cell, the Al foil inside the SIBs remains integrity, but the battery shell has obvious corrosion traces, as shown in Fig. 3g, which is quite different from the result measured by the electrolytic tank as shown in Fig. 3h. From this phenomenon, it can be inferred that NaFSI-E would corrode Al foil as well as stainless steel but corrode stainless steel first.

Battery performance is the most straightly and convincing evidence to evaluate the electrolytes with different sodium salts. At present stage, NFM and HC are widely considered as ideal cathode and anode materials for commercial pouch SIBs due to their duration to water and air $[23–26]$ . The electrochemical performance of NFM||HC pouch SIBs with various electrolytes including $NaPF_{6}$ , NaFSI and NaDFOB from $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ to $70\ ^{\circ}C$ , have been thoroughly investigated. The rate capability of the cells with different electrolytes at various current densities under $45\ ^{\circ}C$ was firstly studied, as illustrated in Fig. 4a. The $NaPF_{6}-E$ and NaFSI-E cells showed similar rate capabilities, while the NaDFOB-E cell exhibited inferior performance. Conversely, the cycling performance as shown in Fig. 4b indicated that the NaDFOB-E and NaFSI-E cells were more stable than the $NaPF_{6}-E$ cell, and following $70\ ^{\circ}C$ storage experiment results also confirmed that NaDFOB-E and NaFSI-E cells had better performance than $NaPF_{6}-E$ cell, as shown in Fig. 4c.

citations.quote: In this work, we have systemically evaluated and compared the discrepancy of SIBs applying different sodium salts from the view of the salt nature themselves, the properties of corresponding electrolytes, the battery performance and characterization analysis. Although $NaPF_{6}$ has been widely applied in SIBs, NaDFOB and NaFSI should also be paid more attention to broaden their application prospects in SIBs. Thereinto, owing to the limited solubility, single NaDFOB is not suitable for low temperature or high concentration electrolyte. The NaDFOB-E electrolyte enables the cells better performance than $NaPF_{6}-E$ , and is not corrosive to Al foil, indicating NaDFOB is a promising salt choice for room and high temperature electrolyte. Benefit to the superior viscosity, conductivity, and SEI/CEI, the low temperature performance of the cells with NaFSI-E is much better than that of other cells, and after solving the corrosion of NaFSI by additive, NaFSI-E is suitable for low temperature application.

evidence_ledger.quote: Sodium hexafluorophosphate (NaPF $_6$ ), ethylene carbonate (EC) and methyl ethyl carbonate (EMC) were supplied by Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. NaPF $_6$ was dissolved into a EC and EMC (EC: EMC = 3:7 in wt.%) mixture to prepare baseline electrolyte (1 mol/L). Trimethylsilyl methanesulfonate additive (97 %, Shanghai Macklin Biochemical Technology Co., Ltd.) was added into the baseline electrolyte to form functional electrolyte. NFM and HC active materials were purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co., Ltd. and Kuraray Co., Ltd., respectively. The NFM cathode was fabricated from NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotubes (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P) and maleic acid dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) at a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated onto an aluminium substrate. The HC anode was contained 95 % HC, 1.5 % carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), 2.0 % styrene butadiene rubber (SBR), and 1.5 % super P. A Celgard 2700 membrane (Xingyuan Materials Co., Ltd) was as the separator. The mass loading of cathode and anode was 33.0 mg cm $^{-2}$ and 20.1 mg cm $^{-2}$ , respectively. The negative-to-positive (N/P) capacity ratio was 1.1. The empty pouch cells were dried under vacuum at 80 °C for 72 h, then transferred to a glove box and injected 6.0 g electrolyte. Other operations not mentioned were all carried out using the general methods in the battery manufacture.

evidence_ledger.quote:
3.1. Design and performance of the functional electrolyte
To begin with, in order to pre-evaluate the practicability of ether and carbonate ester as the electrolyte in pouch cells, comparative tests were first carried out, as shown in Fig. S1. Although the ether electrolytes have a high initial capacity, their cycling stability is poor, with a capacity retention rate of only 77.38 after 105 cycles, while the carbonate electrolytes have a capacity retention rate of 87.49 %. The gas production behaviour of ether and carbonate ester during long-term cycling at a cut-off voltage of 4.0 V at 45°C was monitored using differential electrochemical mass spectrometry (Fig. S2). It was observed that ether produced a greater quantity of gases, including methane and carbon monoxide, in comparison to carbonate ester. This may be a contributing factor to the unsuitability of ether for use in pouch cells, due to the rapid consumption of electrolyte, which results in a rapid decline in battery capacity. The electrolyte formula employs a combination of 1 mol/L NaPF $_{6}$ , cyclic ester EC and linear ester EMC in a mass ratio of 3:7 (called Baseline electrolyte), augmented by the incorporation of 3 wt% TMSS as a functional additive. The introduction of linear esters engenders a reduction in viscosity and an enhanced capacity to dissolve sodium salts in the electrolyte as a whole, thereby facilitating an improvement in the fluidity and ion conductivity of the electrolyte. Compounds containing sulfone groups, such as 1,3-propanesultone (PS), have been demonstrated to have excellent effects in inhibiting gas production and improving high-temperature performance (Fig. 1a). Consequently, they have been introduced into electrolytes and have become widely used. Compounds containing siloxane structures, such as trimethylsilyl isocyanate, exhibit high reactivity due to the facile rupture of their Si-O bonds. This enables effective removal of moisture and acid from the electrolyte and protection of the electrode electrolyte interface phase [25,26]. Therefore, the incorporation of TMSS is anticipated to combine the aforementioned effects with functional electrolytes, thereby achieving high-performance NFM/HC SIBs.

It is well established that sodium-ion batteries exhibit superior low-temperature performance compared to lithium-ion batteries. This attribute is of significant potential value for their future applications $[32]$ . Due to the sluggish interfacial kinetics, the energy density and cycle life of SIBs suffer severely at subzero temperatures $[33]$ . Consequently, the electrochemical performance of electrolytes with and without TMSS was evaluated at extreme temperatures. Fig. 3c illustrates that the electrolyte containing TMSS exhibited superior cycling stability and capacity retention compared to the baseline electrolyte at $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ with a 0.3C charge and 0.5C discharge. Batteries without TMSS exhibited a significant decline in capacity, retaining only 60% of their initial capacity after 40 cycles. This was attributed to their low coulombic efficiency and high polarization.

evidence_ledger.chunk_id: 0030_Li 等 - 2025 - An electrolyte design strategy for commercial all-climate pouch sodium-ion batteries::sec2::child0
evidence_ledger.paper_id: 0030_Li 等 - 2025 - An electrolyte design strategy for commercial all-climate pouch sodium-ion batteries
evidence_ledger.quote: A type of wide temperature range electrolyte design strategy incorporating trifunctional trimethylsilyl methanesulfonate (TMSS) additive in specific carbonate ester is developed to enhance the all-climate performance of commercial pouch $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). The incorporation of TMSS serves optimizing the solvation structure to accelerate the reaction kinetics, eliminating residual $H_{2}O/HF$ from the electrolyte, and promoting the formation of high-quality interface films. The capacity retention of the pouch NFM/HC cells with TMSS is effectively enhanced at high-voltage of 4.0 V and wide-temperature range from $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . The cell delivers a high capacity retention of 80 % after 700 cycles at $25\ ^{\circ}C$ , while the initial energy density is as high as 117 Wh kg $^{-1}$ and maintains 103 Wh kg $^{-1}$ after 300 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ and 1C (1C = 900 mA), achieving an 18.2 % increase in energy density. In addition, no obvious gas evolution can be observed when pouch cell is stored at $60\ ^{\circ}C$ and the low-temperature discharge at $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ achieves a 14.76 % increase in capacity at 0.5C. This work demonstrates the feasibility of TMSS in SIBs, and also put insight on the rational electrolyte design of SIBs.

evidence_ledger.paper_id: 0017_Fan 等 - 2026 - Difluorophosphate-based electrolyte for pouch sodium-ion batteries with a wide temperature range
evidence_ledger.quote: Based on the coupling of difluorophosphate-group with -tris(trimethylsilyl)-group of tris(trimethylsilyl)difluorophosphate (TDFP) additive and a “formation-repair” film-forming strategy, a difluorophosphate-based functional electrolyte is developed. This electrolyte facilitates the formation of tough and rich-NaF interfacial films on two electrodes and achieves an enhanced temperature performance of $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) over a wide range from $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . Compared to the cells without TDFP, the capacity retention of pouch NFM/HC cells with TDFP after 400 cycles at $25\ ^{\circ}C$ increases from 0% to 90%, stable cycling performance is obtained after 150 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ , and even the discharge capacity at $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ and the capacity retention after storage at $60\ ^{\circ}C$ are also greatly improved. In addition, the unique properties of TDFP differ from sodium difluorophosphate (NaDFP) and tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphate (TMSP) are analyzed to elucidate the functional mechanisms of TDFP. It is demonstrated that TDFP can not only catalyze the decomposition of $PF_{6}^{-}$ to form NaF-rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI)/cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI) films but also produce $PO_{2}F_{2}^{-}$ to optimize the film composition.

3.2. Performance of the batteries with different electrolytes
The effect of sodium salts on the safety is also an important factor for commercial SIBs, and the corrosion of battery devices is one of the reference bases for sodium salt selection. Fig. 3e and f shows the corrosion results of Al foil in different electrolytes. As is reported at previous research, NaFSI-E would corrode Al foil during cycling so that may cause safety issues where NaDFOB-E and $\mathrm{NaPF_6 - E}$ hardly react. The coin cell was used to evaluate the corrosion of Al foil in different electrolytes. Surprisingly, although it can still observe obvious corrosion products on the glass fiber after cycling with NaFSI-E when measured with the coin cell, the Al foil inside the SIBs remains integrity, but the battery shell has obvious corrosion traces, as shown in Fig. 3g, which is quite different from the result measured by the electrolytic tank as shown in Fig. 3h. From this phenomenon, it can be inferred that NaFSI-E would corrode Al foil as well as stainless steel but corrode stainless steel first.

Battery performance is the most straightly and convincing evidence to evaluate the electrolytes with different sodium salts. At present stage, NFM and HC are widely considered as ideal cathode and anode materials for commercial pouch SIBs due to their duration to water and air $[23–26]$ . The electrochemical performance of NFM||HC pouch SIBs with various electrolytes including $NaPF_{6}$ , NaFSI and NaDFOB from $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ to $70\ ^{\circ}C$ , have been thoroughly investigated. The rate capability of the cells with different electrolytes at various current densities under $45\ ^{\circ}C$ was firstly studied, as illustrated in Fig. 4a. The $NaPF_{6}-E$ and NaFSI-E cells showed similar rate capabilities, while the NaDFOB-E cell exhibited inferior performance. Conversely, the cycling performance as shown in Fig. 4b indicated that the NaDFOB-E and NaFSI-E cells were more stable than the $NaPF_{6}-E$ cell, and following $70\ ^{\circ}C$ storage experiment results also confirmed that NaDFOB-E and NaFSI-E cells had better performance than $NaPF_{6}-E$ cell, as shown in Fig. 4c.

citations.chunk_id: 0017_Fan 等 - 2026 - Difluorophosphate-based electrolyte for pouch sodium-ion batteries with a wide temperature range::sec4::child0
citations.quote: The main raw materials used for preparing functional electrolytes, including ethylene carbonate (EC), ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC), sodium hexafluorophosphate $\left(\mathrm{NaPF}_{6}\right)$ , NaDFP, TMSP and TDFP were provided by the Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. The baseline electrolyte was prepared by dissolving $NaPF_{6}$ in a mixture of EC: EMC = 3:7 to form a concentration of 0.8 mol $L^{-1}$ . Then, 1% (Mass ratio) NaDFP, TDFP, TMSP was added into the baseline electrolyte to prepare corresponding electrolyte. All electrolytes were prepared in a dry argon filled glove box with both moisture and oxygen concentrations below 0.1 ppm. NFM was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co, Ltd., HC was purchased from Kuraray Co Ltd. The pouch test cells with NFM cathode (120 mAh $g^{-1}$ at 0.1C), HC anode (290 mAh $g^{-1}$ at 0.05C), and Celgard 2700 separator were assembled using the conventional assembly method. Thereinto, NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotube (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and Maleic acid were dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) with a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate to prepare the NFM cathode.

citations.chunk_id: 0017_Fan 等 - 2026 - Difluorophosphate-based electrolyte for pouch sodium-ion batteries with a wide temperature range::sec2::child0
citations.quote: Based on the coupling of difluorophosphate-group with -tris(trimethylsilyl)-group of tris(trimethylsilyl)difluorophosphate (TDFP) additive and a “formation-repair” film-forming strategy, a difluorophosphate-based functional electrolyte is developed. This electrolyte facilitates the formation of tough and rich-NaF interfacial films on two electrodes and achieves an enhanced temperature performance of $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) over a wide range from $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . Compared to the cells without TDFP, the capacity retention of pouch NFM/HC cells with TDFP after 400 cycles at $25\ ^{\circ}C$ increases from 0% to 90%, stable cycling performance is obtained after 150 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ , and even the discharge capacity at $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ and the capacity retention after storage at $60\ ^{\circ}C$ are also greatly improved. In addition, the unique properties of TDFP differ from sodium difluorophosphate (NaDFP) and tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphate (TMSP) are analyzed to elucidate the functional mechanisms of TDFP. It is demonstrated that TDFP can not only catalyze the decomposition of $PF_{6}^{-}$ to form NaF-rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI)/cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI) films but also produce $PO_{2}F_{2}^{-}$ to optimize the film composition.

Furthermore, performance tests were conducted at even lower temperatures, and it was found that the cells with TDFP still maintained an 86% discharge capacity retention rate at -30 °C. Low temperature cycling test is followed to further validate the superior performance of TDFP. As illustrated in Fig. 4d, the cell with TDFP exhibited the best cycling stability, followed by TMSP, then NaDFP, and finally the Baseline. It is worth noting that the performance of TMSP and NaDFP batteries under low-temperature cycling was the reverse of that under room-temperature cycling. This suggests that the failure mechanisms of the batteries and the reasons for performance enhancement by additives also differ. The thicknesses of cells haven't visible change before and after cycling, meaning no significant gas generation could be observed under low-temperature conditions (Fig. 4e). This contrasts with the results under room-temperature cycling, leading to the slightly better performance of TMSP-containing cells compared to NaDFP-containing cells under low-temperature conditions.

Due to the sluggish interfacial kinetics, the energy density and cycle life of SIBs suffer severely at subzero temperatures $[33]$ . citations.quote: Sodium hexafluorophosphate (NaPF $_6$ ), ethylene carbonate (EC) and methyl ethyl carbonate (EMC) were supplied by Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. NaPF $_6$ was dissolved into a EC and EMC (EC: EMC = 3:7 in wt.%) mixture to prepare baseline electrolyte (1 mol/L). The negative-to-positive (N/P) capacity ratio was 1.1. The empty pouch cells were dried under vacuum at 80 °C for 72 h, then transferred to a glove box and injected 6.0 g electrolyte. citations.quote:
3.1. Design and performance of the functional electrolyte
To begin with, in order to pre-evaluate the practicability of ether and carbonate ester as the electrolyte in pouch cells, comparative tests were first carried out, as shown in Fig. S1. Although the ether electrolytes have a high initial capacity, their cycling stability is poor, with a capacity retention rate of only 77.38 after 105 cycles, while the carbonate electrolytes have a capacity retention rate of 87.49 %. The gas production behaviour of ether and carbonate ester during long-term cycling at a cut-off voltage of 4.0 V at 45°C was monitored using differential electrochemical mass spectrometry (Fig. S2). It was observed that ether produced a greater quantity of gases, including methane and carbon monoxide, in comparison to carbonate ester. This may be a contributing factor to the unsuitability of ether for use in pouch cells, due to the rapid consumption of electrolyte, which results in a rapid decline in battery capacity. The electrolyte formula employs a combination of 1 mol/L NaPF $_{6}$ , cyclic ester EC and linear ester EMC in a mass ratio of 3:7 (called Baseline electrolyte), augmented by the incorporation of 3 wt% TMSS as a functional additive. The introduction of linear esters engenders a reduction in viscosity and an enhanced capacity to dissolve sodium salts in the electrolyte as a whole, thereby facilitating an improvement in the fluidity and ion conductivity of the electrolyte. Compounds containing sulfone groups, such as 1,3-propanesultone (PS), have been demonstrated to have excellent effects in inhibiting gas production and improving high-temperature performance (Fig. 1a). Consequently, they have been introduced into electrolytes and have become widely used. Compounds containing siloxane structures, such as trimethylsilyl isocyanate, exhibit high reactivity due to the facile rupture of their Si-O bonds. This enables effective removal of moisture and acid from the electrolyte and protection of the electrode electrolyte interface phase [25,26]. Therefore, the incorporation of TMSS is anticipated to combine the aforementioned effects with functional electrolytes, thereby achieving high-performance NFM/HC SIBs.

citations.chunk_id: 0030_Li 等 - 2025 - An electrolyte design strategy for commercial all-climate pouch sodium-ion batteries::sec2::child0
citations.quote: A type of wide temperature range electrolyte design strategy incorporating trifunctional trimethylsilyl methanesulfonate (TMSS) additive in specific carbonate ester is developed to enhance the all-climate performance of commercial pouch $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). The incorporation of TMSS serves optimizing the solvation structure to accelerate the reaction kinetics, eliminating residual $H_{2}O/HF$ from the electrolyte, and promoting the formation of high-quality interface films. The capacity retention of the pouch NFM/HC cells with TMSS is effectively enhanced at high-voltage of 4.0 V and wide-temperature range from $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . The cell delivers a high capacity retention of 80 % after 700 cycles at $25\ ^{\circ}C$ , while the initial energy density is as high as 117 Wh kg $^{-1}$ and maintains 103 Wh kg $^{-1}$ after 300 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ and 1C (1C = 900 mA), achieving an 18.2 % increase in energy density. In addition, no obvious gas evolution can be observed when pouch cell is stored at $60\ ^{\circ}C$ and the low-temperature discharge at $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ achieves a 14.76 % increase in capacity at 0.5C. This work demonstrates the feasibility of TMSS in SIBs, and also put insight on the rational electrolyte design of SIBs.

citations.quote: This allows it to maintain good performance in low temperature conditions. During the charge and discharge process, TMSS is capable of capturing the HF generated by the hydrolysis of $PF_{6}^{-}$ in the solvent due to the presence of trace amounts of water. This protects the positive electrode material from corrosion and reduces the dissolution of transition metal ions. Additionally, the S = O group of the abundant charge carrier can stabilize $PF_{5}$ , reduce the opening of the solvent EC, and thus reduce the gas production of the pouch cells. This ensures that the battery will remain in good working order under conditions of high temperature. Moreover, TMSS exhibits a preferential oxidation and decomposition process, resulting in the formation of low impedance, high ion mobility CEI films and SEI films rich in S-based and Si-based compounds on the cathode and anode surfaces. Using $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ as a comparison, this work systematically evaluates the application potential of $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ , sodium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (NaFSI) and sodium difluoro(oxalato)borate (NaDFOB) from the sodium salt nature, electrolyte properties, and battery performance. In particular, $\mathrm{NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_2}$ /hard carbon (NFM/HC) SIBs with NaDFOB achieve enhanced performance than that with $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ at high temperature (from $88.2\%$ to $92.4\%$ ), while low temperature performance of NaFSI-containing cells is much better than others (from $0\%$ to $85.9\%$ ).

citations.quote:
3.2. Performance of the batteries with different electrolytes
The effect of sodium salts on the safety is also an important factor for commercial SIBs, and the corrosion of battery devices is one of the reference bases for sodium salt selection. Fig. 3e and f shows the corrosion results of Al foil in different electrolytes. As is reported at previous research, NaFSI-E would corrode Al foil during cycling so that may cause safety issues where NaDFOB-E and $\mathrm{NaPF_6 - E}$ hardly react. The coin cell was used to evaluate the corrosion of Al foil in different electrolytes. Surprisingly, although it can still observe obvious corrosion products on the glass fiber after cycling with NaFSI-E when measured with the coin cell, the Al foil inside the SIBs remains integrity, but the battery shell has obvious corrosion traces, as shown in Fig. 3g, which is quite different from the result measured by the electrolytic tank as shown in Fig. 3h. From this phenomenon, it can be inferred that NaFSI-E would corrode Al foil as well as stainless steel but corrode stainless steel first.

Battery performance is the most straightly and convincing evidence to evaluate the electrolytes with different sodium salts. At present stage, NFM and HC are widely considered as ideal cathode and anode materials for commercial pouch SIBs due to their duration to water and air $[23–26]$ . The electrochemical performance of NFM||HC pouch SIBs with various electrolytes including $NaPF_{6}$ , NaFSI and NaDFOB from $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ to $70\ ^{\circ}C$ , have been thoroughly investigated. The rate capability of the cells with different electrolytes at various current densities under $45\ ^{\circ}C$ was firstly studied, as illustrated in Fig. 4a. The $NaPF_{6}-E$ and NaFSI-E cells showed similar rate capabilities, while the NaDFOB-E cell exhibited inferior performance. Conversely, the cycling performance as shown in Fig. 4b indicated that the NaDFOB-E and NaFSI-E cells were more stable than the $NaPF_{6}-E$ cell, and following $70\ ^{\circ}C$ storage experiment results also confirmed that NaDFOB-E and NaFSI-E cells had better performance than $NaPF_{6}-E$ cell, as shown in Fig. 4c.

citations.quote: In this work, we have systemically evaluated and compared the discrepancy of SIBs applying different sodium salts from the view of the salt nature themselves, the properties of corresponding electrolytes, the battery performance and characterization analysis. Although $NaPF_{6}$ has been widely applied in SIBs, NaDFOB and NaFSI should also be paid more attention to broaden their application prospects in SIBs. Thereinto, owing to the limited solubility, single NaDFOB is not suitable for low temperature or high concentration electrolyte. The NaDFOB-E electrolyte enables the cells better performance than $NaPF_{6}-E$ , and is not corrosive to Al foil, indicating NaDFOB is a promising salt choice for room and high temperature electrolyte. Benefit to the superior viscosity, conductivity, and SEI/CEI, the low temperature performance of the cells with NaFSI-E is much better than that of other cells, and after solving the corrosion of NaFSI by additive, NaFSI-E is suitable for low temperature application.

citations.chunk_id: 0017_Fan 等 - 2026 - Difluorophosphate-based electrolyte for pouch sodium-ion batteries with a wide temperature range::sec2::child0
citations.quote: Based on the coupling of difluorophosphate-group with -tris(trimethylsilyl)-group of tris(trimethylsilyl)difluorophosphate (TDFP) additive and a “formation-repair” film-forming strategy, a difluorophosphate-based functional electrolyte is developed. This electrolyte facilitates the formation of tough and rich-NaF interfacial films on two electrodes and achieves an enhanced temperature performance of $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) over a wide range from $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . Compared to the cells without TDFP, the capacity retention of pouch NFM/HC cells with TDFP after 400 cycles at $25\ ^{\circ}C$ increases from 0% to 90%, stable cycling performance is obtained after 150 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ , and even the discharge capacity at $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ and the capacity retention after storage at $60\ ^{\circ}C$ are also greatly improved. In addition, the unique properties of TDFP differ from sodium difluorophosphate (NaDFP) and tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphate (TMSP) are analyzed to elucidate the functional mechanisms of TDFP. It is demonstrated that TDFP can not only catalyze the decomposition of $PF_{6}^{-}$ to form NaF-rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI)/cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI) films but also produce $PO_{2}F_{2}^{-}$ to optimize the film composition.

association_citations.chunk_id: 0017_Fan 等 - 2026 - Difluorophosphate-based electrolyte for pouch sodium-ion batteries with a wide temperature range::sec2::child0
association_citations.quote: Based on the coupling of difluorophosphate-group with -tris(trimethylsilyl)-group of tris(trimethylsilyl)difluorophosphate (TDFP) additive and a “formation-repair” film-forming strategy, a difluorophosphate-based functional electrolyte is developed. This electrolyte facilitates the formation of tough and rich-NaF interfacial films on two electrodes and achieves an enhanced temperature performance of $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) over a wide range from $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . Compared to the cells without TDFP, the capacity retention of pouch NFM/HC cells with TDFP after 400 cycles at $25\ ^{\circ}C$ increases from 0% to 90%, stable cycling performance is obtained after 150 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ , and even the discharge capacity at $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ and the capacity retention after storage at $60\ ^{\circ}C$ are also greatly improved. In addition, the unique properties of TDFP differ from sodium difluorophosphate (NaDFP) and tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphate (TMSP) are analyzed to elucidate the functional mechanisms of TDFP. It is demonstrated that TDFP can not only catalyze the decomposition of $PF_{6}^{-}$ to form NaF-rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI)/cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI) films but also produce $PO_{2}F_{2}^{-}$ to optimize the film composition.

3.1. Design and performance of the functional electrolyte
To begin with, in order to pre-evaluate the practicability of ether and carbonate ester as the electrolyte in pouch cells, comparative tests were first carried out, as shown in Fig. S1. Although the ether electrolytes have a high initial capacity, their cycling stability is poor, with a capacity retention rate of only 77.38 after 105 cycles, while the carbonate electrolytes have a capacity retention rate of 87.49 %. The gas production behaviour of ether and carbonate ester during long-term cycling at a cut-off voltage of 4.0 V at 45°C was monitored using differential electrochemical mass spectrometry (Fig. S2). It was observed that ether produced a greater quantity of gases, including methane and carbon monoxide, in comparison to carbonate ester. This may be a contributing factor to the unsuitability of ether for use in pouch cells, due to the rapid consumption of electrolyte, which results in a rapid decline in battery capacity. The electrolyte formula employs a combination of 1 mol/L NaPF $_{6}$ , cyclic ester EC and linear ester EMC in a mass ratio of 3:7 (called Baseline electrolyte), augmented by the incorporation of 3 wt% TMSS as a functional additive. The introduction of linear esters engenders a reduction in viscosity and an enhanced capacity to dissolve sodium salts in the electrolyte as a whole, thereby facilitating an improvement in the fluidity and ion conductivity of the electrolyte. Compounds containing sulfone groups, such as 1,3-propanesultone (PS), have been demonstrated to have excellent effects in inhibiting gas production and improving high-temperature performance (Fig. 1a). Consequently, they have been introduced into electrolytes and have become widely used. Compounds containing siloxane structures, such as trimethylsilyl isocyanate, exhibit high reactivity due to the facile rupture of their Si-O bonds. This enables effective removal of moisture and acid from the electrolyte and protection of the electrode electrolyte interface phase [25,26]. Therefore, the incorporation of TMSS is anticipated to combine the aforementioned effects with functional electrolytes, thereby achieving high-performance NFM/HC SIBs.

citations.chunk_id: 0030_Li 等 - 2025 - An electrolyte design strategy for commercial all-climate pouch sodium-ion batteries::sec2::child0
citations.quote: A type of wide temperature range electrolyte design strategy incorporating trifunctional trimethylsilyl methanesulfonate (TMSS) additive in specific carbonate ester is developed to enhance the all-climate performance of commercial pouch $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). The incorporation of TMSS serves optimizing the solvation structure to accelerate the reaction kinetics, eliminating residual $H_{2}O/HF$ from the electrolyte, and promoting the formation of high-quality interface films. The capacity retention of the pouch NFM/HC cells with TMSS is effectively enhanced at high-voltage of 4.0 V and wide-temperature range from $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . The cell delivers a high capacity retention of 80 % after 700 cycles at $25\ ^{\circ}C$ , while the initial energy density is as high as 117 Wh kg $^{-1}$ and maintains 103 Wh kg $^{-1}$ after 300 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ and 1C (1C = 900 mA), achieving an 18.2 % increase in energy density. In addition, no obvious gas evolution can be observed when pouch cell is stored at $60\ ^{\circ}C$ and the low-temperature discharge at $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ achieves a 14.76 % increase in capacity at 0.5C. This work demonstrates the feasibility of TMSS in SIBs, and also put insight on the rational electrolyte design of SIBs.

association_citations.quote:
The main raw materials used for preparing functional electrolytes, including EC, EMC, $NaPF_{6}$ , NaDFP, TMSP and TMSB were provided by the Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. The baseline electrolyte was prepared by dissolving $NaPF_{6}$ in a mixture of EC: EMC=3:7 to form a concentration of 0.8 mol $L^{-1}$ . Then, NaDFP was added into the baseline electrolyte to prepare the NaDFP electrolyte, and NaDFP and

TMSB or TMSP were respectively added into the baseline electrolyte and assigned as NB or NP electrolyte. All electrolytes were prepared in a dry argon filled glove box with both moisture and oxygen concentrations below 0.1 ppm. NFM was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co, Ltd, HC was purchased from Kuraray Co Ltd. The pouch test cells with NFM cathode (120 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.1 C), HC anode (290 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.05 C), and Celgard 2700 separator were assembled using the conventional assembly method. Therein, NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotube (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and Maleic acid (the reason of addition maleic acid was shown in Table 1) were dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) with a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate to prepare the NFM cathode.

association_citations.quote: With the help of "hard-soft synergy", polarization and capacity fading are alleviated signally during the cycling. Besides, rate performance of pouch cells is also improved by the synergistic effect of NP or NB electrolyte even at $-10^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and $1\mathrm{C}$ , as shown in Fig. 4d and S5b. Furthermore, to evaluate dual additive potential at tougher low-temperatures, $-20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and $-30^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ discharge tests are necessary. Fig. 4e shows the capacity retention of pouch cells at different discharge currents, revealing the cells all can exhibit good electrochemical performance under the tested temperature conditions. Even at $-30^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and $1\mathrm{C}$ , the discharge capacity of pouch cells with NP and NB electrolytes still achieves $729\mathrm{mAh}$ and $697\mathrm{mAh}$ , respectively. These results confirm that this co-additive addition strategy improves extremely low temperature performance of NFM/HC pouch cells. Summarily, compared to single additive or baseline electrolyte, NFM/HC pouch cells with multi-component functional electrolyte possess much better performance. Therein, the cells containing NP electrolyte have better room and high-temperature performance, and the cells containing NB electrolyte are more suitable for low-temperature application.

citations.quote: Sodium salts in the electrolytes are key materials for developing high-performance sodium ion batteries (SIBs) due to their direct influences on the electrode reactions and electrolyte conductivity, and sodium fluorophosphate $(\mathrm{NaPF}_6)$ is known to be widely applied. Using $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ as a comparison, this work systematically evaluates the application potential of $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ , sodium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (NaFSI) and sodium difluoro(oxalato)borate (NaDFOB) from the sodium salt nature, electrolyte properties, and battery performance. It is demonstrated that NaFSI can exhibit excellent comprehensive performance and has the potential to substitute for $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ under certain conditions; NaDFOB is more suitable as an additive to improve the high-temperature performance of SIBs. In particular, $\mathrm{NaNi_{1/3}Fe_{1/3}Mn_{1/3}O_2}$ /hard carbon (NFM/HC) SIBs with NaDFOB achieve enhanced performance than that with $\mathrm{NaPF_6}$ at high temperature (from $88.2\%$ to $92.4\%$ ), while low temperature performance of NaFSI-containing cells is much better than others (from $0\%$ to $85.9\%$ ).

citations.quote: Besides, the physicochemical properties of three electrolytes containing NaDFOB (NaDFOB-E), $NaPF_{6}$ ( $NaPF_{6}-E$ ), and NaFSI (NaFSI-E) were measured. The solubility of three salts at different temperatures in the commonly used commercial solvent combinations (EC/EMC = 1:1) was tested. It was indicated that the solubility of NaDFOB was significantly lower than that of the other two salts, as shown in Fig. 1c and Fig. S1, indicating NaDFOB might not be suitable for high concentration or low temperature electrolyte as a main salt. Thus, the 0.8 M electrolytes containing different sodium salts were further investigated. The LSV curves of the electrolytes in the voltage range of 2.0–5.5 V (vs. Na/Na $^{+}$ ) were used to evaluate the electrochemical stable window (ESW) of electrolytes. As shown in Fig. 1d, no obvious oxidation current peaks were observed in NaPF $_{6}$ -E and NaDFOB-E below 4.5 V. The oxidation current peak of NaFSI-E increased far more sharply when the voltage exceeded 4.0 V, which might be attributed to the instability of FSI $^{-}$ anions under higher voltage. The density of three electrolytes (0.8 M) is shown in Fig. 1e, where injection amount of NaFSI-E might much more than other. In addition, the viscosity and conductivity are also important properties for commercial electrolyte, which deeply affects the performance of SIBs, especially at the low temperature.

citations.quote:
3.2. Performance of the batteries with different electrolytes
The effect of sodium salts on the safety is also an important factor for commercial SIBs, and the corrosion of battery devices is one of the reference bases for sodium salt selection. Fig. 3e and f shows the corrosion results of Al foil in different electrolytes. As is reported at previous research, NaFSI-E would corrode Al foil during cycling so that may cause safety issues where NaDFOB-E and $\mathrm{NaPF_6 - E}$ hardly react. The coin cell was used to evaluate the corrosion of Al foil in different electrolytes. Surprisingly, although it can still observe obvious corrosion products on the glass fiber after cycling with NaFSI-E when measured with the coin cell, the Al foil inside the SIBs remains integrity, but the battery shell has obvious corrosion traces, as shown in Fig. 3g, which is quite different from the result measured by the electrolytic tank as shown in Fig. 3h. From this phenomenon, it can be inferred that NaFSI-E would corrode Al foil as well as stainless steel but corrode stainless steel first.

Battery performance is the most straightly and convincing evidence to evaluate the electrolytes with different sodium salts. At present stage, NFM and HC are widely considered as ideal cathode and anode materials for commercial pouch SIBs due to their duration to water and air $[23–26]$ . The electrochemical performance of NFM||HC pouch SIBs with various electrolytes including $NaPF_{6}$ , NaFSI and NaDFOB from $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ to $70\ ^{\circ}C$ , have been thoroughly investigated. The rate capability of the cells with different electrolytes at various current densities under $45\ ^{\circ}C$ was firstly studied, as illustrated in Fig. 4a. The $NaPF_{6}-E$ and NaFSI-E cells showed similar rate capabilities, while the NaDFOB-E cell exhibited inferior performance. Conversely, the cycling performance as shown in Fig. 4b indicated that the NaDFOB-E and NaFSI-E cells were more stable than the $NaPF_{6}-E$ cell, and following $70\ ^{\circ}C$ storage experiment results also confirmed that NaDFOB-E and NaFSI-E cells had better performance than $NaPF_{6}-E$ cell, as shown in Fig. 4c.

requirements.reasoning: sec11::child0 concludes NaFSI-E is suitable for low temperature only 'after solving the corrosion of NaFSI by additive'; the candidate specifies no additives, so the as-formulated electrolyte does not meet the suitability claim as stated.

citations.chunk_id: 0016_Fan 等 - 2025 - Electrolyte salts for large-scale application of sodium-ion batteries NaPF6 and emerging alternativ::sec11::child0
citations.quote: In this work, we have systemically evaluated and compared the discrepancy of SIBs applying different sodium salts from the view of the salt nature themselves, the properties of corresponding electrolytes, the battery performance and characterization analysis. Although $NaPF_{6}$ has been widely applied in SIBs, NaDFOB and NaFSI should also be paid more attention to broaden their application prospects in SIBs. Thereinto, owing to the limited solubility, single NaDFOB is not suitable for low temperature or high concentration electrolyte. The NaDFOB-E electrolyte enables the cells better performance than $NaPF_{6}-E$ , and is not corrosive to Al foil, indicating NaDFOB is a promising salt choice for room and high temperature electrolyte. Benefit to the superior viscosity, conductivity, and SEI/CEI, the low temperature performance of the cells with NaFSI-E is much better than that of other cells, and after solving the corrosion of NaFSI by additive, NaFSI-E is suitable for low temperature application.

review.experimental_association: The corrosion and low-temperature results are tied to NFM||HC pouch cells with the same electrolyte family (NaFSI-E), as sec9::child1/child4 describe the pouch cell tests and sec9::child0 reports shell/Al corrosion on the pouch cell, so the corrosion observation and cycling data belong to the same target cell configuration rather than a different system.

association_citations.quote: At present stage, NFM and HC are widely considered as ideal cathode and anode materials for commercial pouch SIBs due to their duration to water and air $[23–26]$ . The electrochemical performance of NFM||HC pouch SIBs with various electrolytes including $NaPF_{6}$ , NaFSI and NaDFOB from $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ to $70\ ^{\circ}C$ , have been thoroughly investigated. The rate capability of the cells with different electrolytes at various current densities under $45\ ^{\circ}C$ was firstly studied, as illustrated in Fig. 4a. The $NaPF_{6}-E$ and NaFSI-E cells showed similar rate capabilities, while the NaDFOB-E cell exhibited inferior performance.

Surprisingly, although it can still observe obvious corrosion products on the glass fiber after cycling with NaFSI-E when measured with the coin cell, the Al foil inside the SIBs remains integrity, but the battery shell has obvious corrosion traces, as shown in Fig. 3g, which is

review.recommendation_reason: The candidate satisfies the concentration/solvent identity and the -10 °C NFM||HC low-temperature performance (90 % retention after 200 cycles). However, the program's mandatory condition of no observed collector/shell corrosion is refuted: the paper observes obvious stainless-steel shell corrosion and infers Al corrosion for NaFSI-E, and states NaFSI-E is only suitable for low temperature after corrosion is solved by an additive, which this additive-free candidate lacks. Therefore the electrolyte cannot be recommended as-is; decision is held pending a formulation that resolves the shell/collector corrosion.

## 配方筛选结果
已整理候选资料，当前暂缓推荐。未满足的条件列在下方。

### 候选资料：C1-TDFP-0017（尚未获推荐）
以下为候选记录中的组成，配制时须核对所引原文的比例基准与用量。
盐：NaPF6；浓度：0.8 mol L⁻¹；溶剂：EC, EMC；溶剂比例（基准待核对）：EC=3.0, EMC=7.0；添加剂：TDFP；添加剂用量：TDFP=1% mass ratio in the baseline electrolyte。
- 配方原文 [0017_Fan 等 - 2026 - Difluorophosphate-based electrolyte for pouch sodium-ion batteries with a wide temperature range::sec4::child0]：The main raw materials used for preparing functional electrolytes, including ethylene carbonate (EC), ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC), sodium hexafluorophosphate $\left(\mathrm{NaPF}_{6}\right)$ , NaDFP, TMSP and TDFP were provided by the Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. The baseline electrolyte was prepared by dissolving $NaPF_{6}$ in a mixture of EC: EMC = 3:7 to form a concentration of 0.8 mol $L^{-1}$ . Then, 1% (Mass ratio) NaDFP, TDFP, TMSP was added into the baseline electrolyte to prepare corresponding electrolyte. All electrolytes were prepared in a dry argon filled glove box with both moisture and oxygen concentrations below 0.1 ppm. NFM was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co, Ltd., HC was purchased from Kuraray Co Ltd. The pouch test cells with NFM cathode (120 mAh $g^{-1}$ at 0.1C), HC anode (290 mAh $g^{-1}$ at 0.05C), and Celgard 2700 separator were assembled using the conventional assembly method. Thereinto, NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotube (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and Maleic acid were dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) with a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate to prepare the NFM cathode.

### 候选资料：C2-TMSS-0030（尚未获推荐）
以下为候选记录中的组成，配制时须核对所引原文的比例基准与用量。
盐：NaPF6；浓度：1 mol L⁻¹；溶剂：EC, EMC；溶剂比例（质量）：EC=3.0, EMC=7.0；添加剂：TMSS；添加剂用量：TMSS=3 wt% in the electrolyte。
- 配方原文 [0030_Li 等 - 2025 - An electrolyte design strategy for commercial all-climate pouch sodium-ion batteries::sec4::child0]：Sodium hexafluorophosphate (NaPF $_6$ ), ethylene carbonate (EC) and methyl ethyl carbonate (EMC) were supplied by Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. NaPF $_6$ was dissolved into a EC and EMC (EC: EMC = 3:7 in wt.%) mixture to prepare baseline electrolyte (1 mol/L). Trimethylsilyl methanesulfonate additive (97 %, Shanghai Macklin Biochemical Technology Co., Ltd.) was added into the baseline electrolyte to form functional electrolyte. NFM and HC active materials were purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co., Ltd. and Kuraray Co., Ltd., respectively. The NFM cathode was fabricated from NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotubes (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P) and maleic acid dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) at a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated onto an aluminium substrate. The HC anode was contained 95 % HC, 1.5 % carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), 2.0 % styrene butadiene rubber (SBR), and 1.5 % super P. A Celgard 2700 membrane (Xingyuan Materials Co., Ltd) was as the separator. The mass loading of cathode and anode was 33.0 mg cm $^{-2}$ and 20.1 mg cm $^{-2}$ , respectively. The negative-to-positive (N/P) capacity ratio was 1.1. The empty pouch cells were dried under vacuum at 80 °C for 72 h, then transferred to a glove box and injected 6.0 g electrolyte. Other operations not mentioned were all carried out using the general methods in the battery manufacture.
- 配方原文 [0030_Li 等 - 2025 - An electrolyte design strategy for commercial all-climate pouch sodium-ion batteries::sec7]：3.1. Design and performance of the functional electrolyte
To begin with, in order to pre-evaluate the practicability of ether and carbonate ester as the electrolyte in pouch cells, comparative tests were first carried out, as shown in Fig. S1. Although the ether electrolytes have a high initial capacity, their cycling stability is poor, with a capacity retention rate of only 77.38 after 105 cycles, while the carbonate electrolytes have a capacity retention rate of 87.49 %. The gas production behaviour of ether and carbonate ester during long-term cycling at a cut-off voltage of 4.0 V at 45°C was monitored using differential electrochemical mass spectrometry (Fig. S2). It was observed that ether produced a greater quantity of gases, including methane and carbon monoxide, in comparison to carbonate ester. This may be a contributing factor to the unsuitability of ether for use in pouch cells, due to the rapid consumption of electrolyte, which results in a rapid decline in battery capacity. The electrolyte formula employs a combination of 1 mol/L NaPF $_{6}$ , cyclic ester EC and linear ester EMC in a mass ratio of 3:7 (called Baseline electrolyte), augmented by the incorporation of 3 wt% TMSS as a functional additive. The introduction of linear esters engenders a reduction in viscosity and an enhanced capacity to dissolve sodium salts in the electrolyte as a whole, thereby facilitating an improvement in the fluidity and ion conductivity of the electrolyte. Compounds containing sulfone groups, such as 1,3-propanesultone (PS), have been demonstrated to have excellent effects in inhibiting gas production and improving high-temperature performance (Fig. 1a). Consequently, they have been introduced into electrolytes and have become widely used. Compounds containing siloxane structures, such as trimethylsilyl isocyanate, exhibit high reactivity due to the facile rupture of their Si-O bonds. This enables effective removal of moisture and acid from the electrolyte and protection of the electrode electrolyte interface phase [25,26]. Therefore, the incorporation of TMSS is anticipated to combine the aforementioned effects with functional electrolytes, thereby achieving high-performance NFM/HC SIBs.

The potential function of TMSS in the electrolyte is also evaluated through DFT theoretical calculations. Fig. 1b lists the HOMO and LUMO energy levels of a series of molecul

### 候选资料：C3-NB-0156（尚未获推荐）
以下为候选记录中的组成，配制时须核对所引原文的比例基准与用量。
盐：NaPF6；浓度：0.8 mol L⁻¹；溶剂：EC, EMC；溶剂比例（基准待核对）：EC=3.0, EMC=7.0；添加剂：NaDFP, TMSB；添加剂用量：NaDFP=NaDFP:TMSB = 1:1.5 ratio stated; absolute dosage not stated in retrieved text, TMSB=NaDFP:TMSB = 1:1.5 ratio stated; absolute dosage not stated in retrieved text。
- 配方原文 [0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec4::child0]：The main raw materials used for preparing functional electrolytes, including EC, EMC, $NaPF_{6}$ , NaDFP, TMSP and TMSB were provided by the Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. The baseline electrolyte was prepared by dissolving $NaPF_{6}$ in a mixture of EC: EMC=3:7 to form a concentration of 0.8 mol $L^{-1}$ . Then, NaDFP was added into the baseline electrolyte to prepare the NaDFP electrolyte, and NaDFP and

TMSB or TMSP were respectively added into the baseline electrolyte and assigned as NB or NP electrolyte. All electrolytes were prepared in a dry argon filled glove box with both moisture and oxygen concentrations below 0.1 ppm. NFM was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co, Ltd, HC was purchased from Kuraray Co Ltd. The pouch test cells with NFM cathode (120 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.1 C), HC anode (290 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.05 C), and Celgard 2700 separator were assembled using the conventional assembly method. Therein, NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotube (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and Maleic acid (the reason of addition maleic acid was shown in Table 1) were dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) with a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate to prepare the NFM cathode.
- 配方原文 [0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec8::child0]：Taking into account the application environment temperature and corresponding performance requirements of the SIBs, the performance parameters of pouch cells under different temperature conditions after adding different electrolytes were evaluated in a targeted manner. In order to choose the optimal concentration, part of the tough condition performance corresponding to different addition amounts of two additives is shown in Fig. S3. Considering cost and performance comprehensively, a 1:1.5 proportioning of NaDFP to TMSB or TMSB is chosen as the most suitable ratio. First, under the room and high temperatures, the emphasis of pouch cells with different electrolytes was given to the rate, cycling and storage performance parameters. The pouch cells with NB, NP, or NaDFP-containing electrolytes generally exhibit higher performance parameters than the cells with the baseline electrolyte. Under the room temperature of 25 °C, as shown in the Fig. S4a and S4b, rate and cycling performance of the pouch cells with the NB and NP-containing electrolytes is improved comparing to the cells with the baseline electrolyte, which can easily ascribed to the superior conductivity and lower desolvation energy. To further verify the effect of NP, NB, and NaDFP electrolytes at tougher conditions, rate, cycling, and storage tests at 45 °C and 60 °C were performed.

### 候选资料：C4-NaPF6E-0016（尚未获推荐）
以下为候选记录中的组成，配制时须核对所引原文的比例基准与用量。
盐：NaPF6；浓度：0.8 mol L⁻¹；溶剂：EC, EMC；溶剂比例（基准待核对）：EC=1.0, EMC=1.0。
- 配方原文 [0016_Fan 等 - 2025 - Electrolyte salts for large-scale application of sodium-ion batteries NaPF6 and emerging alternativ::sec8::child2]：Besides, the physicochemical properties of three electrolytes containing NaDFOB (NaDFOB-E), $NaPF_{6}$ ( $NaPF_{6}-E$ ), and NaFSI (NaFSI-E) were measured. The solubility of three salts at different temperatures in the commonly used commercial solvent combinations (EC/EMC = 1:1) was tested. It was indicated that the solubility of NaDFOB was significantly lower than that of the other two salts, as shown in Fig. 1c and Fig. S1, indicating NaDFOB might not be suitable for high concentration or low temperature electrolyte as a main salt. Thus, the 0.8 M electrolytes containing different sodium salts were further investigated. The LSV curves of the electrolytes in the voltage range of 2.0–5.5 V (vs. Na/Na $^{+}$ ) were used to evaluate the electrochemical stable window (ESW) of electrolytes. As shown in Fig. 1d, no obvious oxidation current peaks were observed in NaPF $_{6}$ -E and NaDFOB-E below 4.5 V. The oxidation current peak of NaFSI-E increased far more sharply when the voltage exceeded 4.0 V, which might be attributed to the instability of FSI $^{-}$ anions under higher voltage. The density of three electrolytes (0.8 M) is shown in Fig. 1e, where injection amount of NaFSI-E might much more than other. In addition, the viscosity and conductivity are also important properties for commercial electrolyte, which deeply affects the performance of SIBs, especially at the low temperature.

盐：NaFSI；浓度：0.8 mol L⁻¹；溶剂：EC, EMC；溶剂比例（基准待核对）：EC=1.0, EMC=1.0。

## 候选评估
### C1-TDFP-0017
评估建议：The candidate matches the paper's TDFP electrolyte and is well supported for -10 °C NFM/HC pouch performance, but the program's explicit no-corrosion requirement (Al collector/stainless-steel shell) has no direct negative evidence in the sources, so a held decision is warranted pending corrosion data.
任务要求与已有依据（模型语义判断，程序核验出处）：
- Pouch NFM||hard-carbon cell format matching the target system：The source describes pouch test cells assembled with an NFM cathode and HC anode, i.e. the same full-cell configuration as the target cell. [0017_Fan 等 - 2026 - Difluorophosphate-based electrolyte for pouch sodium-ion batteries with a wide temperature range::sec4::child0]
- Electrolyte identity: 0.8 mol/L NaPF6 in EC:EMC = 3:7 with 1% mass TDFP：The baseline electrolyte is stated as NaPF6 at 0.8 mol/L in EC:EMC = 3:7, and 1% (mass ratio) TDFP is added to it, matching the candidate composition exactly. [0017_Fan 等 - 2026 - Difluorophosphate-based electrolyte for pouch sodium-ion batteries with a wide temperature range::sec4::child0]
- Low-temperature (-10 °C) performance of the TDFP electrolyte in NFM/HC pouch cells：The paper reports low-temperature rate/discharge/cycling of pouch NFM/HC cells and states the TDFP cells showed the best cycling stability at low temperature, including improved discharge performance at sub-zero conditions. [0017_Fan 等 - 2026 - Difluorophosphate-based electrolyte for pouch sodium-ion batteries with a wide temperature range::sec2::child0][0017_Fan 等 - 2026 - Difluorophosphate-based electrolyte for pouch sodium-ion batteries with a wide temperature range::sec7::child11][0017_Fan 等 - 2026 - Difluorophosphate-based electrolyte for pouch sodium-ion batteries with a wide temperature range::sec7::child12]
- Al current collector in the target cell：The NFM cathode slurry is described as coated on an aluminum substrate, confirming Al as the cathode current collector. [0017_Fan 等 - 2026 - Difluorophosphate-based electrolyte for pouch sodium-ion batteries with a wide temperature range::sec4::child0]
- Stainless-steel shell in the target cell：No source chunk describes the cell casing/shell material, so the stainless-steel shell requirement is not addressed. 
- No observed corrosion of the Al current collector or stainless-steel shell with the TDFP electrolyte：The sources report no direct negative corrosion observation for the Al collector or steel shell; only positive anode-plating suppression and general cycling data are given, which cannot establish the required negative fact. 
文献与候选的关联：The candidate composition (0.8 M NaPF6, EC:EMC 3:7, 1% TDFP) is identical to the paper's TDFP functional electrolyte, which was evaluated in pouch NFM/HC cells including low-temperature (-10 °C) cycling; the source therefore supplies directly relevant full-cell low-temperature evidence for this candidate, though it does not test collector/shell corrosion. [0017_Fan 等 - 2026 - Difluorophosphate-based electrolyte for pouch sodium-ion batteries with a wide temperature range::sec4::child0][0017_Fan 等 - 2026 - Difluorophosphate-based electrolyte for pouch sodium-ion batteries with a wide temperature range::sec2::child0]
### C2-TMSS-0030
评估建议：The candidate's composition and -10 °C pouch NFM/HC performance are directly supported, but the program's hard requirement of no observed Al-collector or stainless-steel-shell corrosion is not evidenced (both are insufficient), so a recommendation cannot be issued and the decision is held pending direct corrosion observations.
任务要求与已有依据（模型语义判断，程序核验出处）：
- Electrolyte supports NFM||hard-carbon pouch-cell cycling at -10 °C：The source directly reports pouch NFM/HC cells cycled at -10 °C with 0.3C charge/0.5C discharge in 1.5–3.8 V, where the TMSS-containing electrolyte gave superior cycling stability and capacity retention versus baseline. [0030_Li 等 - 2025 - An electrolyte design strategy for commercial all-climate pouch sodium-ion batteries::sec7::child13]
- Salt/solvent/additive identity matches 1 mol/L NaPF6, EC:EMC 3:7 by mass, plus 3 wt% TMSS：The preparation section states NaPF6 dissolved in EC:EMC = 3:7 wt.% to make 1 mol/L baseline, with trimethylsilyl methanesulfonate added to form the functional electrolyte; the design section confirms 3 wt% TMSS. [0030_Li 等 - 2025 - An electrolyte design strategy for commercial all-climate pouch sodium-ion batteries::sec4::child0][0030_Li 等 - 2025 - An electrolyte design strategy for commercial all-climate pouch sodium-ion batteries::sec7]
- Target cell is a pouch NFM/HC sodium-ion cell：The abstract and results describe commercial pouch NaNi0.33Fe0.33Mn0.33O2 (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) cells with the TMSS electrolyte. [0030_Li 等 - 2025 - An electrolyte design strategy for commercial all-climate pouch sodium-ion batteries::sec2::child0][0030_Li 等 - 2025 - An electrolyte design strategy for commercial all-climate pouch sodium-ion batteries::sec7::child13]
- No observed corrosion of the Al current collector in this candidate electrolyte：The source notes the NFM slurry was coated onto an aluminium substrate and that TMSS protects the positive-electrode material from HF corrosion / reduces transition-metal dissolution, but it never reports a direct observation of Al-current-collector corrosion (or its absence) in this candidate; cathode-material protection is not the same as Al-foil corrosion observation. [0030_Li 等 - 2025 - An electrolyte design strategy for commercial all-climate pouch sodium-ion batteries::sec4::child0][0030_Li 等 - 2025 - An electrolyte design strategy for commercial all-climate pouch sodium-ion batteries::sec8::child8]
- No observed corrosion of the stainless-steel shell：No source chunk mentions a stainless-steel shell or any observation of shell corrosion/absence of corrosion; this required negative fact is unsupported. 
文献与候选的关联：The sources link the exact candidate chemistry (1 mol/L NaPF6 in EC:EMC 3:7 wt% with 3 wt% TMSS) to pouch NFM/HC cells built with an Al-coated NFM cathode, and report -10 °C cycling superiority for the TMSS electrolyte; the same work attributes this to HF/H2O scavenging and interface-film formation. This association supports low-temperature performance and composition identity, but the corrosion requirement is about a different observed quantity (collector/shell corrosion) that the source does not report, so the association does not extend to proving the no-corrosion condition. [0030_Li 等 - 2025 - An electrolyte design strategy for commercial all-climate pouch sodium-ion batteries::sec4::child0][0030_Li 等 - 2025 - An electrolyte design strategy for commercial all-climate pouch sodium-ion batteries::sec7::child13][0030_Li 等 - 2025 - An electrolyte design strategy for commercial all-climate pouch sodium-ion batteries::sec8::child8]
### C3-NB-0156
评估建议：The NB candidate matches the required salt/solvent/additive identity and is directly supported for -10 °C NFM||HC pouch-cell operation, but the program's hard requirement of no observed Al-collector or stainless-steel shell corrosion has no supporting (or negative) evidence, so the decision is held pending corrosion data.
任务要求与已有依据（模型语义判断，程序核验出处）：
- Salt system is NaPF6 at 0.8 mol L^-1 in EC:EMC = 3:7 (candidate electrolyte identity)：The baseline electrolyte is NaPF6 dissolved in EC:EMC=3:7 to 0.8 mol L^-1, and NB is this baseline with NaDFP+TMSB added, matching the candidate composition. [0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec4::child0]
- Additive package is NaDFP with TMSB in a 1:1.5 ratio (candidate identity)：The paper states a 1:1.5 proportioning of NaDFP to TMSB was chosen as the most suitable ratio, and assigns this combination as the NB electrolyte. [0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec8::child0]
- Cell is a NFM cathode || hard-carbon anode pouch cell：Pouch test cells were assembled with NFM cathode, HC anode and described pouch format, matching the target chemistry. [0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec4::child0]
- Al current collector is used：The NFM cathode slurry is coated on an aluminum substrate, confirming an Al current collector is present in the tested cells. [0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec4::child0]
- Electrolyte supports -10 °C low-temperature operation：The paper reports -10 °C, 1C performance of pouch cells and states NB electrolyte is more suitable for low-temperature application due to reduced desolvation energy and viscosity. [0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec8::child3][0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec2::child1]
- Cell has a stainless-steel shell：Sources describe pouch test cells and an Al substrate but never mention a stainless-steel shell or casing material, so this identity element is not evidenced. 
- No observed corrosion of the Al current collector：No corrosion observation or test on the Al collector is reported; normal cycling or good performance cannot establish a negative corrosion finding. 
- No observed corrosion of the stainless-steel shell：No shell material is identified and no corrosion test for a stainless-steel shell is reported, so a negative corrosion result is unsupported. 
文献与候选的关联：The candidate's NB electrolyte (NaPF6/EC:EMC 3:7 0.8 M + NaDFP-TMSB 1:1.5) is the same formulation whose NFM||HC pouch-cell data at low temperature are reported, and the cathode is coated on Al, so the low-temperature and electrode-format evidence transfers directly; however, no corrosion assessment on the collector or any shell is included. [0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec4::child0][0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec8::child3]
### C4-NaPF6E-0016
评估建议：评估已完成：候选 C4-NaPF6E-0016 在盐身份、0.8 M 浓度、EC/EMC 溶剂及 Al 集流体无腐蚀方面与文献条件一致，但目标 -10 °C 低温性能被原文直接反证（NaPF6-E 在 -10 °C、1C 下 50 圈后容量骤降），且不锈钢外壳无腐蚀缺乏针对该候选的直接阴性证据，因此不推荐，建议 hold。

- Electrolyte salt identity: NaPF6：来源明确以 NaPF6-E (NaPF6 电解液) 为三种被比较盐之一，候选盐身份与文献对象一致。 [0016_Fan 等 - 2025 - Electrolyte salts for large-scale application of sodium-ion batteries NaPF6 and emerging alternativ::sec3::child0]
